personae.name: SATURNINUS
personae.blurb: elder son to the late Emperor of Rome, afterwards Emperor

personae.name: TITUS ANDRONICUS
personae.blurb: a noble Roman, General against the Goths

personae.name: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
personae.blurb: Tribune of the People, and brother to Titus

lines.text: Enter the Tribunes and Senators aloft. And then enter Saturninus and his followers at one door, and Bassianus and his followers at the other, with drums and trumpets.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Noble patricians, patrons of my right,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Defend the justice of my cause with arms;

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: And, countrymen, my loving followers,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Plead my successive title with your swords.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: I am his firstborn son that was the last

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: That wore the imperial diadem of Rome;

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Then let my father’s honours live in me,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Nor wrong mine age with this indignity.

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Romans, friends, followers, favourers of my right,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: If ever Bassianus, Caesar’s son,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Were gracious in the eyes of royal Rome,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Keep then this passage to the Capitol,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: And suffer not dishonour to approach

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: The imperial seat, to virtue consecrate,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: To justice, continence, and nobility;

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: But let desert in pure election shine,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: And, Romans, fight for freedom in your choice.
Enter Marcus Andronicus aloft, holding the crown.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Princes, that strive by factions and by friends

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Ambitiously for rule and empery,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Know that the people of Rome, for whom we stand

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: A special party, have by common voice,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: In election for the Roman empery,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Chosen Andronicus, surnamed Pius

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: For many good and great deserts to Rome.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: A nobler man, a braver warrior,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Lives not this day within the city walls.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: He by the senate is accited home

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: From weary wars against the barbarous Goths,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: That with his sons, a terror to our foes,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Hath yoked a nation strong, trained up in arms.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Ten years are spent since first he undertook

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: This cause of Rome, and chastised with arms

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Our enemies’ pride. Five times he hath returned

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Bleeding to Rome, bearing his valiant sons

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: In coffins from the field.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And now at last, laden with honour’s spoils,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Returns the good Andronicus to Rome,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Renowned Titus, flourishing in arms.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Let us entreat, by honour of his name

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Whom worthily you would have now succeed,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And in the Capitol and senate’s right,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Whom you pretend to honour and adore,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: That you withdraw you and abate your strength,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Dismiss your followers, and, as suitors should,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Plead your deserts in peace and humbleness.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: How fair the tribune speaks to calm my thoughts!

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Marcus Andronicus, so I do affy

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: In thy uprightness and integrity,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: And so I love and honour thee and thine,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Thy noble brother Titus and his sons,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: And her to whom my thoughts are humbled all,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Gracious Lavinia, Rome’s rich ornament,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: That I will here dismiss my loving friends,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: And to my fortunes and the people’s favour

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Commit my cause in balance to be weighed.
[_Exeunt the followers of Bassianus._]

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Friends, that have been thus forward in my right,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: I thank you all and here dismiss you all,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: And to the love and favour of my country

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Commit myself, my person, and the cause.
[_Exeunt the followers of Saturninus._]

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Rome, be as just and gracious unto me

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: As I am confident and kind to thee.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Open the gates and let me in.

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Tribunes, and me, a poor competitor.
[_Flourish. They go up into the Senate House._]
Enter a Captain.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Romans, make way! The good Andronicus,

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Patron of virtue, Rome’s best champion,

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Successful in the battles that he fights,

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: With honour and with fortune is returned

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: From where he circumscribed with his sword

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: And brought to yoke the enemies of Rome.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Sound drums and trumpets, and then enter two of Titus’ sons, and then

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: two men bearing a coffin covered with black; then two other sons; then

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Titus Andronicus; and then Tamora, the Queen of Goths and her sons

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Alarbus, Chiron and Demetrius with Aaron the Moor, and others as many

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: as can be, then set down the coffin, and Titus speaks.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Hail, Rome, victorious in thy mourning weeds!

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Lo, as the bark that hath discharged her fraught

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Returns with precious lading to the bay

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: From whence at first she weighed her anchorage,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Cometh Andronicus, bound with laurel boughs,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: To resalute his country with his tears,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Tears of true joy for his return to Rome.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Thou great defender of this Capitol,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Stand gracious to the rites that we intend.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Romans, of five-and-twenty valiant sons,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Half of the number that King Priam had,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Behold the poor remains, alive and dead.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: These that survive let Rome reward with love;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: These that I bring unto their latest home,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: With burial amongst their ancestors.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Here Goths have given me leave to sheathe my sword.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Titus, unkind, and careless of thine own,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Why suffer’st thou thy sons, unburied yet,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: To hover on the dreadful shore of Styx?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Make way to lay them by their brethren.
[_They open the tomb._]

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: There greet in silence, as the dead are wont,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And sleep in peace, slain in your country’s wars.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: O sacred receptacle of my joys,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Sweet cell of virtue and nobility,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: How many sons hast thou of mine in store,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: That thou wilt never render to me more?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Give us the proudest prisoner of the Goths,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: That we may hew his limbs, and on a pile

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: _Ad manes fratrum_ sacrifice his flesh

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Before this earthy prison of their bones,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: That so the shadows be not unappeased,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Nor we disturbed with prodigies on earth.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: I give him you, the noblest that survives,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: The eldest son of this distressed queen.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Stay, Roman brethren! Gracious conqueror,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Victorious Titus, rue the tears I shed,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: A mother’s tears in passion for her son.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And if thy sons were ever dear to thee,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: O, think my son to be as dear to me.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Sufficeth not that we are brought to Rome,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: To beautify thy triumphs and return

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Captive to thee and to thy Roman yoke;

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: But must my sons be slaughtered in the streets

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: For valiant doings in their country’s cause?

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: O, if to fight for king and commonweal

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Were piety in thine, it is in these.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Andronicus, stain not thy tomb with blood.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Wilt thou draw near the nature of the gods?

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Draw near them then in being merciful.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Sweet mercy is nobility’s true badge.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Thrice-noble Titus, spare my first-born son.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Patient yourself, madam, and pardon me.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: These are their brethren whom your Goths beheld

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Alive and dead, and for their brethren slain

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Religiously they ask a sacrifice.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: To this your son is marked, and die he must,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: T’ appease their groaning shadows that are gone.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Away with him, and make a fire straight,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And with our swords, upon a pile of wood,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Let’s hew his limbs till they be clean consumed.
[_Exeunt Titus’ sons with Alarbus._]

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: O cruel, irreligious piety!

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: Was never Scythia half so barbarous!

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Oppose not Scythia to ambitious Rome.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Alarbus goes to rest, and we survive

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: To tremble under Titus’ threat’ning look.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Then, madam, stand resolved, but hope withal

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: The self-same gods that armed the Queen of Troy

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: With opportunity of sharp revenge

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Upon the Thracian tyrant in his tent

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: May favour Tamora, the queen of Goths,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: (When Goths were Goths and Tamora was queen)

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: To quit the bloody wrongs upon her foes.
Enter the sons of Andronicus again with bloody swords.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: See, lord and father, how we have performed

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Our Roman rites. Alarbus’ limbs are lopped,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And entrails feed the sacrificing fire,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Whose smoke like incense doth perfume the sky.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Remaineth naught but to inter our brethren,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And with loud ’larums welcome them to Rome.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Let it be so; and let Andronicus

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Make this his latest farewell to their souls.
[_Sound trumpets, and lay the coffin in the tomb._]

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: In peace and honour rest you here, my sons;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Rome’s readiest champions, repose you here in rest,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Secure from worldly chances and mishaps.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Here lurks no treason, here no envy swells,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Here grow no damned drugs; here are no storms,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: No noise, but silence and eternal sleep.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: In peace and honour rest you here, my sons.
Enter Lavinia.

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: In peace and honour live Lord Titus long;

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: My noble lord and father, live in fame.

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: Lo, at this tomb my tributary tears

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: I render for my brethren’s obsequies;

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: And at thy feet I kneel, with tears of joy

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: Shed on this earth for thy return to Rome.

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: O, bless me here with thy victorious hand,

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: Whose fortunes Rome’s best citizens applaud.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Kind Rome, that hast thus lovingly reserved

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: The cordial of mine age to glad my heart!

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Lavinia, live; outlive thy father’s days,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And fame’s eternal date, for virtue’s praise.
Enter Marcus Andronicus and Tribunes; re-enter Saturninus, Bassianus and others.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Long live Lord Titus, my beloved brother,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Gracious triumpher in the eyes of Rome.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Thanks, gentle tribune, noble brother Marcus.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And welcome, nephews, from successful wars,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: You that survive, and you that sleep in fame.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Fair lords, your fortunes are alike in all,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: That in your country’s service drew your swords;

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: But safer triumph is this funeral pomp

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: That hath aspired to Solon’s happiness

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And triumphs over chance in honour’s bed.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Titus Andronicus, the people of Rome,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Whose friend in justice thou hast ever been,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Send thee by me, their tribune and their trust,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: This palliament of white and spotless hue,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And name thee in election for the empire

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: With these our late-deceased emperor’s sons.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Be _candidatus_ then, and put it on,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And help to set a head on headless Rome.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: A better head her glorious body fits

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Than his that shakes for age and feebleness.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: What, should I don this robe and trouble you?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Be chosen with proclamations today,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Tomorrow yield up rule, resign my life,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And set abroad new business for you all?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Rome, I have been thy soldier forty years,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And led my country’s strength successfully,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And buried one and twenty valiant sons,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Knighted in field, slain manfully in arms,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: In right and service of their noble country.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Give me a staff of honour for mine age,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: But not a sceptre to control the world.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Upright he held it, lords, that held it last.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Titus, thou shalt obtain and ask the empery.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Proud and ambitious tribune, canst thou tell?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Patience, Prince Saturninus.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Romans, do me right.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Patricians, draw your swords, and sheathe them not

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Till Saturninus be Rome’s emperor.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Andronicus, would thou were shipped to hell

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Rather than rob me of the people’s hearts!

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Proud Saturnine, interrupter of the good

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: That noble-minded Titus means to thee!

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Content thee, prince; I will restore to thee

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: The people’s hearts, and wean them from themselves.

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Andronicus, I do not flatter thee,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: But honour thee, and will do till I die.

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: My faction if thou strengthen with thy friends,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: I will most thankful be; and thanks to men

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Of noble minds is honourable meed.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: People of Rome, and people’s tribunes here,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: I ask your voices and your suffrages.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Will you bestow them friendly on Andronicus?

lines.speaker: TRIBUNES
lines.text: To gratify the good Andronicus,

lines.speaker: TRIBUNES
lines.text: And gratulate his safe return to Rome,

lines.speaker: TRIBUNES
lines.text: The people will accept whom he admits.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Tribunes, I thank you; and this suit I make,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: That you create your emperor’s eldest son,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Lord Saturnine; whose virtues will, I hope,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Reflect on Rome as Titan’s rays on earth,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And ripen justice in this commonweal.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Then, if you will elect by my advice,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Crown him, and say “Long live our emperor!”

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: With voices and applause of every sort,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Patricians and plebeians, we create

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Lord Saturninus Rome’s great emperor,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And say “Long live our Emperor Saturnine!”
[_A long flourish._]

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Titus Andronicus, for thy favours done

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: To us in our election this day,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: I give thee thanks in part of thy deserts,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: And will with deeds requite thy gentleness.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: And for an onset, Titus, to advance

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Thy name and honourable family,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Lavinia will I make my empress,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Rome’s royal mistress, mistress of my heart,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: And in the sacred Pantheon her espouse.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Tell me, Andronicus, doth this motion please thee?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: It doth, my worthy lord, and in this match

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: I hold me highly honoured of your grace;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And here in sight of Rome, to Saturnine,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: King and commander of our commonweal,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: The wide world’s emperor, do I consecrate

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: My sword, my chariot, and my prisoners;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Presents well worthy Rome’s imperious lord.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Receive them then, the tribute that I owe,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Mine honour’s ensigns humbled at thy feet.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Thanks, noble Titus, father of my life.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: How proud I am of thee and of thy gifts

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Rome shall record, and when I do forget

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: The least of these unspeakable deserts,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Romans, forget your fealty to me.
[_To Tamora_.]

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Now, madam, are you prisoner to an emperor;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: To him that for your honour and your state

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Will use you nobly and your followers.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: A goodly lady, trust me, of the hue

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: That I would choose, were I to choose anew.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Clear up, fair queen, that cloudy countenance.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Though chance of war hath wrought this change of cheer,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Thou com’st not to be made a scorn in Rome.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Princely shall be thy usage every way.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Rest on my word, and let not discontent

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Daunt all your hopes. Madam, he comforts you

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Can make you greater than the Queen of Goths.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Lavinia, you are not displeased with this?

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: Not I, my lord, sith true nobility

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: Warrants these words in princely courtesy.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Thanks, sweet Lavinia. Romans, let us go.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Ransomless here we set our prisoners free.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Proclaim our honours, lords, with trump and drum.
[_Flourish. Saturninus and his Guards exit, with Drums and Trumpets.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Tribunes and Senators exit aloft._]

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Lord Titus, by your leave, this maid is mine.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: How, sir? Are you in earnest then, my lord?

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Ay, noble Titus; and resolved withal

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: To do myself this reason and this right.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: _Suum cuique_ is our Roman justice.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: This prince in justice seizeth but his own.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And that he will and shall, if Lucius live.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Traitors, avaunt! Where is the emperor’s guard?
Enter Saturninus and his Guards.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Treason, my lord, Lavinia is surprised.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Surprised? By whom?

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: By him that justly may

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Bear his betrothed from all the world away.
[_Exeunt Bassianus and Marcus with Lavinia._]

lines.speaker: MUTIUS
lines.text: Brothers, help to convey her hence away,

lines.speaker: MUTIUS
lines.text: And with my sword I’ll keep this door safe.
[_Exeunt Lucius, Quintus and Martius._]

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Follow, my lord, and I’ll soon bring her back.
[_Exeunt Saturninus, Tamora, Demetrius, Chiron, Aaron, and Guards._]

lines.speaker: MUTIUS
lines.text: My lord, you pass not here.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: What, villain boy,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Barr’st me my way in Rome?
[_Stabbing Mutius._]

lines.speaker: MUTIUS
lines.text: Help, Lucius, help!
[_Dies._]
Re-enter Lucius.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: My lord, you are unjust, and more than so,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: In wrongful quarrel you have slain your son.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Nor thou nor he are any sons of mine;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: My sons would never so dishonour me.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Traitor, restore Lavinia to the Emperor.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Dead, if you will; but not to be his wife,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: That is another’s lawful promised love.
[_Exit._]
Enter aloft the Emperor Saturninus with Tamora and her two sons and Aaron the Moor.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: No, Titus, no; the emperor needs her not,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Nor her, nor thee, nor any of thy stock.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: I’ll trust by leisure him that mocks me once;

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Thee never, nor thy traitorous haughty sons,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Confederates all thus to dishonour me.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Was none in Rome to make a stale

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: But Saturnine? Full well, Andronicus,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Agree these deeds with that proud brag of thine

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: That said’st I begged the empire at thy hands.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: O monstrous! What reproachful words are these?

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: But go thy ways; go, give that changing piece

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: To him that flourished for her with his sword.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: A valiant son-in-law thou shalt enjoy;

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: One fit to bandy with thy lawless sons,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: To ruffle in the commonwealth of Rome.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: These words are razors to my wounded heart.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: And therefore, lovely Tamora, Queen of Goths,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: That like the stately Phœbe ’mongst her nymphs

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Dost overshine the gallant’st dames of Rome,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: If thou be pleased with this my sudden choice,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Behold, I choose thee, Tamora, for my bride,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: And will create thee Empress of Rome.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Speak, Queen of Goths, dost thou applaud my choice?

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: And here I swear by all the Roman gods,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Sith priest and holy water are so near,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: And tapers burn so bright, and everything

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: In readiness for Hymenæus stand,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: I will not re-salute the streets of Rome,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Or climb my palace, till from forth this place

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: I lead espoused my bride along with me.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And here in sight of heaven to Rome I swear,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: If Saturnine advance the Queen of Goths,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: She will a handmaid be to his desires,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: A loving nurse, a mother to his youth.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Ascend, fair queen, Pantheon. Lords, accompany

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Your noble emperor and his lovely bride,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Sent by the heavens for Prince Saturnine,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Whose wisdom hath her fortune conquered.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: There shall we consummate our spousal rites.
[_Exeunt all but Titus._]

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: I am not bid to wait upon this bride.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Titus, when wert thou wont to walk alone,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Dishonoured thus, and challenged of wrongs?
Re-enter Marcus, Lucius, Quintus and Martius.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: O Titus, see, O, see what thou hast done!

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: In a bad quarrel slain a virtuous son.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: No, foolish tribune, no; no son of mine,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Nor thou, nor these, confederates in the deed

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: That hath dishonoured all our family.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Unworthy brother and unworthy sons!

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: But let us give him burial, as becomes;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Give Mutius burial with our brethren.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Traitors, away! He rests not in this tomb.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: This monument five hundred years hath stood,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Which I have sumptuously re-edified.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Here none but soldiers and Rome’s servitors

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Repose in fame; none basely slain in brawls.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Bury him where you can, he comes not here.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: My lord, this is impiety in you.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: My nephew Mutius’ deeds do plead for him;

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: He must be buried with his brethren.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: And shall, or him we will accompany.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: “And shall”? What villain was it spake that word?

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: He that would vouch it in any place but here.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: What, would you bury him in my despite?

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: No, noble Titus, but entreat of thee

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: To pardon Mutius and to bury him.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Marcus, even thou hast struck upon my crest,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And with these boys mine honour thou hast wounded.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: My foes I do repute you every one;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: So trouble me no more, but get you gone.

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: He is not with himself; let us withdraw.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Not I, till Mutius’ bones be buried.
[_Marcus and the sons of Titus kneel._]

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Brother, for in that name doth nature plead,—

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: Father, and in that name doth nature speak,—

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Speak thou no more, if all the rest will speed.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Renowned Titus, more than half my soul,—

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Dear father, soul and substance of us all,—

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Suffer thy brother Marcus to inter

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: His noble nephew here in virtue’s nest,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: That died in honour and Lavinia’s cause.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Thou art a Roman; be not barbarous.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: The Greeks upon advice did bury Ajax,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: That slew himself; and wise Laertes’ son

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Did graciously plead for his funerals.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Let not young Mutius, then, that was thy joy,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Be barred his entrance here.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Rise, Marcus, rise.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: The dismall’st day is this that e’er I saw,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: To be dishonoured by my sons in Rome!

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Well, bury him, and bury me the next.
[_They put Mutius in the tomb._]

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: There lie thy bones, sweet Mutius, with thy friends,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Till we with trophies do adorn thy tomb.
[_Kneeling_.]

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: No man shed tears for noble Mutius;

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: He lives in fame that died in virtue’s cause.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: My lord, to step out of these dreary dumps,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: How comes it that the subtle Queen of Goths

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Is of a sudden thus advanced in Rome?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: I know not, Marcus, but I know it is.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Whether by device or no, the heavens can tell.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Is she not then beholding to the man

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: That brought her for this high good turn so far?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Yes, and will nobly him remunerate.
Flourish. Enter the Emperor Saturninus, Tamora and her two sons, with Aaron the Moor. Drums and Trumpets, at one door. Enter at the other door Bassianus and Lavinia with others.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: So, Bassianus, you have played your prize.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: God give you joy, sir, of your gallant bride.

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: And you of yours, my lord. I say no more,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Nor wish no less; and so I take my leave.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Traitor, if Rome have law or we have power,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Thou and thy faction shall repent this rape.

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Rape call you it, my lord, to seize my own,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: My true betrothed love, and now my wife?

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: But let the laws of Rome determine all;

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Meanwhile am I possessed of that is mine.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: ’Tis good, sir. You are very short with us;

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: But if we live, we’ll be as sharp with you.

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: My lord, what I have done, as best I may,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Answer I must, and shall do with my life.

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Only thus much I give your grace to know:

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: By all the duties that I owe to Rome,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: This noble gentleman, Lord Titus here,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Is in opinion and in honour wronged,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: That, in the rescue of Lavinia,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: With his own hand did slay his youngest son,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: In zeal to you, and highly moved to wrath

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: To be controlled in that he frankly gave.

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Receive him then to favour, Saturnine,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: That hath expressed himself in all his deeds

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: A father and a friend to thee and Rome.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Prince Bassianus, leave to plead my deeds.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: ’Tis thou, and those, that have dishonoured me.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Rome and the righteous heavens be my judge

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: How I have loved and honoured Saturnine.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: My worthy lord, if ever Tamora

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Were gracious in those princely eyes of thine,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Then hear me speak indifferently for all;

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And at my suit, sweet, pardon what is past.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: What, madam, be dishonoured openly,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: And basely put it up without revenge?

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Not so, my lord; the gods of Rome forfend

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: I should be author to dishonour you!

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: But on mine honour dare I undertake

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: For good Lord Titus’ innocence in all,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Whose fury not dissembled speaks his griefs.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Then at my suit look graciously on him;

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Lose not so noble a friend on vain suppose,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Nor with sour looks afflict his gentle heart.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: My lord, be ruled by me, be won at last;

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Dissemble all your griefs and discontents.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: You are but newly planted in your throne;

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Lest, then, the people, and patricians too,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Upon a just survey take Titus’ part,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And so supplant you for ingratitude,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Which Rome reputes to be a heinous sin,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Yield at entreats, and then let me alone.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: I’ll find a day to massacre them all,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And raze their faction and their family,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: The cruel father and his traitorous sons,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: To whom I sued for my dear son’s life;

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And make them know what ’tis to let a queen

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Kneel in the streets and beg for grace in vain.
[_Aloud_.]

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Come, come, sweet emperor; come, Andronicus;

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Take up this good old man, and cheer the heart

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: That dies in tempest of thy angry frown.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Rise, Titus, rise; my empress hath prevailed.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: I thank your majesty and her, my lord.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: These words, these looks, infuse new life in me.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Titus, I am incorporate in Rome,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: A Roman now adopted happily,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And must advise the emperor for his good.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: This day all quarrels die, Andronicus;

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And let it be mine honour, good my lord,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: That I have reconciled your friends and you.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: For you, Prince Bassianus, I have passed

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: My word and promise to the emperor

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: That you will be more mild and tractable.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And fear not, lords, and you, Lavinia.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: By my advice, all humbled on your knees,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: You shall ask pardon of his majesty.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: We do, and vow to heaven and to his highness

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: That what we did was mildly as we might,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Tend’ring our sister’s honour and our own.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: That on mine honour here do I protest.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Away, and talk not; trouble us no more.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Nay, nay, sweet emperor, we must all be friends.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: The tribune and his nephews kneel for grace;

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: I will not be denied. Sweet heart, look back.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Marcus, for thy sake, and thy brother’s here,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: And at my lovely Tamora’s entreats,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: I do remit these young men’s heinous faults.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Stand up.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Lavinia, though you left me like a churl,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: I found a friend, and sure as death I swore

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: I would not part a bachelor from the priest.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Come, if the emperor’s court can feast two brides,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: You are my guest, Lavinia, and your friends.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: This day shall be a love-day, Tamora.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Tomorrow, an it please your majesty

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: To hunt the panther and the hart with me,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: With horn and hound we’ll give your grace _bonjour_.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Be it so, Titus, and gramercy too.
[_Sound trumpets. Exeunt all but Aaron._]
Aaron alone.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Now climbeth Tamora Olympus’ top,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Safe out of Fortune’s shot, and sits aloft,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Secure of thunder’s crack or lightning’s flash,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Advanced above pale envy’s threat’ning reach.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: As when the golden sun salutes the morn,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And, having gilt the ocean with his beams,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Gallops the zodiac in his glistening coach,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And overlooks the highest-peering hills;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: So Tamora.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Upon her wit doth earthly honour wait,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And virtue stoops and trembles at her frown.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Then, Aaron, arm thy heart and fit thy thoughts

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: To mount aloft with thy imperial mistress,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And mount her pitch, whom thou in triumph long

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Hast prisoner held, fett’red in amorous chains,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And faster bound to Aaron’s charming eyes

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Than is Prometheus tied to Caucasus.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Away with slavish weeds and servile thoughts!

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: I will be bright, and shine in pearl and gold,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: To wait upon this new-made empress.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: To wait, said I? To wanton with this queen,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: This goddess, this Semiramis, this nymph,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: This siren, that will charm Rome’s Saturnine,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And see his shipwrack and his commonweal’s.

lines.text: Chiron, thy years wants wit, thy wit wants edge

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: And manners, to intrude where I am graced,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: And may, for aught thou knowest, affected be.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: Demetrius, thou dost overween in all,

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: And so in this, to bear me down with braves.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: ’Tis not the difference of a year or two

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: Makes me less gracious or thee more fortunate.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: I am as able and as fit as thou

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: To serve and to deserve my mistress’ grace;

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: And that my sword upon thee shall approve,

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: And plead my passions for Lavinia’s love.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Clubs, clubs! These lovers will not keep the peace.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Why, boy, although our mother, unadvised,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Gave you a dancing-rapier by your side,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Are you so desperate grown to threat your friends?

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Go to; have your lath glued within your sheath

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Till you know better how to handle it.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: Meanwhile, sir, with the little skill I have,

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: Full well shalt thou perceive how much I dare.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Ay, boy, grow ye so brave?
[_They draw._]

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Why, how now, lords!

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: So near the emperor’s palace dare ye draw,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And maintain such a quarrel openly?

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Full well I wot the ground of all this grudge.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: I would not for a million of gold

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: The cause were known to them it most concerns;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Nor would your noble mother for much more

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Be so dishonoured in the court of Rome.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: For shame, put up.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Not I, till I have sheathed

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: My rapier in his bosom, and withal

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Thrust those reproachful speeches down his throat

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: That he hath breathed in my dishonour here.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: For that I am prepared and full resolved,

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: Foul-spoken coward, that thund’rest with thy tongue,

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: And with thy weapon nothing dar’st perform.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Away, I say!

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Now, by the gods that warlike Goths adore,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: This pretty brabble will undo us all.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Why, lords, and think you not how dangerous

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: It is to jet upon a prince’s right?

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: What, is Lavinia then become so loose,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Or Bassianus so degenerate,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: That for her love such quarrels may be broached

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Without controlment, justice, or revenge?

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Young lords, beware! And should the empress know

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: This discord’s ground, the music would not please.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: I care not, I, knew she and all the world.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: I love Lavinia more than all the world.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Youngling, learn thou to make some meaner choice.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Lavina is thine elder brother’s hope.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Why, are ye mad? Or know ye not in Rome

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: How furious and impatient they be,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And cannot brook competitors in love?

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: I tell you, lords, you do but plot your deaths

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: By this device.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: Aaron, a thousand deaths

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: Would I propose to achieve her whom I love.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: To achieve her! How?

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Why makes thou it so strange?

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: She is a woman, therefore may be wooed;

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: She is a woman, therefore may be won;

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: She is Lavinia, therefore must be loved.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: What, man, more water glideth by the mill

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Than wots the miller of; and easy it is

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Of a cut loaf to steal a shive, we know.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Though Bassianus be the emperor’s brother,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Better than he have worn Vulcan’s badge.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Ay, and as good as Saturninus may.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Then why should he despair that knows to court it

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: With words, fair looks, and liberality?

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: What, hast not thou full often struck a doe,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: And borne her cleanly by the keeper’s nose?

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Why, then, it seems some certain snatch or so

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Would serve your turns.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: Ay, so the turn were served.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Aaron, thou hast hit it.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Would you had hit it too!

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Then should not we be tired with this ado.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Why, hark ye, hark ye, and are you such fools

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: To square for this? Would it offend you then

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: That both should speed?

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: Faith, not me.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Nor me, so I were one.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: For shame, be friends, and join for that you jar.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: ’Tis policy and stratagem must do

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: That you affect; and so must you resolve

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: That what you cannot as you would achieve,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: You must perforce accomplish as you may.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Take this of me: Lucrece was not more chaste

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Than this Lavinia, Bassianus’ love.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: A speedier course than ling’ring languishment

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Must we pursue, and I have found the path.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: My lords, a solemn hunting is in hand;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: There will the lovely Roman ladies troop.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: The forest walks are wide and spacious,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And many unfrequented plots there are

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Fitted by kind for rape and villainy.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Single you thither, then, this dainty doe,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And strike her home by force, if not by words.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: This way, or not at all, stand you in hope.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Come, come, our empress, with her sacred wit

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: To villainy and vengeance consecrate,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Will we acquaint with all what we intend;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And she shall file our engines with advice

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: That will not suffer you to square yourselves,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: But to your wishes’ height advance you both.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: The emperor’s court is like the house of Fame,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: The palace full of tongues, of eyes and ears;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: The woods are ruthless, dreadful, deaf, and dull.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: There speak and strike, brave boys, and take your turns;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: There serve your lust, shadowed from heaven’s eye,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And revel in Lavinia’s treasury.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: Thy counsel, lad, smells of no cowardice.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: _Sit fas aut nefas_, till I find the stream

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: To cool this heat, a charm to calm these fits,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: _Per Stygia, per manes vehor._
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: A Forest near Rome; a Lodge seen at a distance. Horns and cry

lines.text: of hounds heard
Enter Titus Andronicus and his three sons, and Marcus, making a noise with hounds and horns.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: The hunt is up, the morn is bright and grey,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: The fields are fragrant, and the woods are green.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Uncouple here, and let us make a bay,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And wake the emperor and his lovely bride,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And rouse the prince, and ring a hunter’s peal,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: That all the court may echo with the noise.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Sons, let it be your charge, as it is ours,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: To attend the emperor’s person carefully.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: I have been troubled in my sleep this night,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: But dawning day new comfort hath inspired.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Here a cry of hounds, and wind horns in a peal. Then enter Saturninus,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Tamora, Bassianus, Lavinia, Chiron, Demetrius, and their Attendants.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Many good morrows to your majesty;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Madam, to you as many and as good.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: I promised your grace a hunter’s peal.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: And you have rung it lustily, my lords;

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Somewhat too early for new-married ladies.

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Lavinia, how say you?

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: I say no;

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: I have been broad awake two hours and more.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Come on then; horse and chariots let us have,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: And to our sport. [_To Tamora_.] Madam, now shall ye see

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Our Roman hunting.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: I have dogs, my lord,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Will rouse the proudest panther in the chase,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And climb the highest promontory top.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And I have horse will follow where the game

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Makes way, and run like swallows o’er the plain.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Chiron, we hunt not, we, with horse nor hound,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: But hope to pluck a dainty doe to ground.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: A lonely part of the Forest

lines.text: Enter Aaron, alone, carrying a bag of gold.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: He that had wit would think that I had none,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: To bury so much gold under a tree,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And never after to inherit it.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Let him that thinks of me so abjectly

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Know that this gold must coin a stratagem,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Which, cunningly effected, will beget

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: A very excellent piece of villainy.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And so repose, sweet gold, for their unrest

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: That have their alms out of the empress’ chest.
[_He hides the bag._]
Enter Tamora alone to the Moor.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: My lovely Aaron, wherefore look’st thou sad

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: When everything doth make a gleeful boast?

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: The birds chant melody on every bush,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: The snakes lie rolled in the cheerful sun,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: The green leaves quiver with the cooling wind,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And make a chequered shadow on the ground.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Under their sweet shade, Aaron, let us sit,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And whilst the babbling echo mocks the hounds,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Replying shrilly to the well-tuned horns,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: As if a double hunt were heard at once,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Let us sit down and mark their yelping noise;

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And after conflict such as was supposed

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: The wand’ring prince and Dido once enjoyed,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: When with a happy storm they were surprised,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And curtained with a counsel-keeping cave,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: We may, each wreathed in the other’s arms,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Our pastimes done, possess a golden slumber,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Whiles hounds and horns and sweet melodious birds

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Be unto us as is a nurse’s song

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Of lullaby to bring her babe asleep.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Madam, though Venus govern your desires,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Saturn is dominator over mine.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: What signifies my deadly-standing eye,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: My silence and my cloudy melancholy,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: My fleece of woolly hair that now uncurls

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Even as an adder when she doth unroll

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: To do some fatal execution?

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: No, madam, these are no venereal signs.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Vengeance is in my heart, death in my hand,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Blood and revenge are hammering in my head.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Hark, Tamora, the empress of my soul,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Which never hopes more heaven than rests in thee,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: This is the day of doom for Bassianus;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: His Philomel must lose her tongue today,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Thy sons make pillage of her chastity,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And wash their hands in Bassianus’ blood.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Seest thou this letter? Take it up, I pray thee,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And give the king this fatal-plotted scroll.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Now question me no more; we are espied;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Here comes a parcel of our hopeful booty,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Which dreads not yet their lives’ destruction.
Enter Bassianus and Lavinia.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Ah, my sweet Moor, sweeter to me than life!

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: No more, great empress. Bassianus comes.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Be cross with him; and I’ll go fetch thy sons

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: To back thy quarrels, whatsoe’er they be.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Who have we here? Rome’s royal empress,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Unfurnished of her well-beseeming troop?

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Or is it Dian, habited like her,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Who hath abandoned her holy groves

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: To see the general hunting in this forest?

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Saucy controller of my private steps!

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Had I the power that some say Dian had,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Thy temples should be planted presently

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: With horns, as was Actaeon’s; and the hounds

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Should drive upon thy new-transformed limbs,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Unmannerly intruder as thou art.

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: Under your patience, gentle empress,

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: ’Tis thought you have a goodly gift in horning,

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: And to be doubted that your Moor and you

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: Are singled forth to try experiments.

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: Jove shield your husband from his hounds today!

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: ’Tis pity they should take him for a stag.

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Believe me, queen, your swarthy Cimmerian

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Doth make your honour of his body’s hue,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Spotted, detested, and abominable.

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Why are you sequestered from all your train,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Dismounted from your snow-white goodly steed,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: And wandered hither to an obscure plot,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: Accompanied but with a barbarous Moor,

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: If foul desire had not conducted you?

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: And, being intercepted in your sport,

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: Great reason that my noble lord be rated

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: For sauciness. I pray you, let us hence,

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: And let her joy her raven-coloured love;

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: This valley fits the purpose passing well.

lines.speaker: BASSIANUS
lines.text: The king my brother shall have notice of this.

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: Ay, for these slips have made him noted long.

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: Good king, to be so mightily abused!

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Why, I have patience to endure all this.
Enter Chiron and Demetrius.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: How now, dear sovereign, and our gracious mother!

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Why doth your highness look so pale and wan?

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Have I not reason, think you, to look pale?

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: These two have ticed me hither to this place,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: A barren detested vale you see it is;

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: The trees, though summer, yet forlorn and lean,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Overcome with moss and baleful mistletoe.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Here never shines the sun, here nothing breeds,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Unless the nightly owl or fatal raven.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And when they showed me this abhorred pit,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: They told me, here, at dead time of the night,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: A thousand fiends, a thousand hissing snakes,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Ten thousand swelling toads, as many urchins,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Would make such fearful and confused cries

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: As any mortal body hearing it

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Should straight fall mad, or else die suddenly.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: No sooner had they told this hellish tale

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: But straight they told me they would bind me here

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Unto the body of a dismal yew,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And leave me to this miserable death.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And then they called me foul adulteress,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Lascivious Goth, and all the bitterest terms

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: That ever ear did hear to such effect.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And had you not by wondrous fortune come,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: This vengeance on me had they executed.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Revenge it, as you love your mother’s life,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Or be ye not henceforth called my children.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: This is a witness that I am thy son.
[_Stabs Bassianus._]

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: And this for me, struck home to show my strength.
[_Also stabs Bassianus, who dies._]

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: Ay, come, Semiramis, nay, barbarous Tamora,

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: For no name fits thy nature but thy own!

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Give me thy poniard; you shall know, my boys,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Your mother’s hand shall right your mother’s wrong.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Stay, madam, here is more belongs to her.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: First thrash the corn, then after burn the straw.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: This minion stood upon her chastity,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Upon her nuptial vow, her loyalty,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: And with that painted hope braves your mightiness;

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: And shall she carry this unto her grave?

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: And if she do, I would I were an eunuch.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: Drag hence her husband to some secret hole,

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: And make his dead trunk pillow to our lust.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: But when ye have the honey ye desire,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Let not this wasp outlive, us both to sting.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: I warrant you, madam, we will make that sure.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: Come, mistress, now perforce we will enjoy

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: That nice-preserved honesty of yours.

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: O Tamora, thou bearest a woman’s face,—

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: I will not hear her speak; away with her!

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: Sweet lords, entreat her hear me but a word.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Listen, fair madam: let it be your glory

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: To see her tears; but be your heart to them

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: As unrelenting flint to drops of rain.

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: When did the tiger’s young ones teach the dam?

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: O, do not learn her wrath; she taught it thee;

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: The milk thou suck’st from her did turn to marble;

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: Even at thy teat thou hadst thy tyranny.

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: Yet every mother breeds not sons alike.
[_To Chiron_.]

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: Do thou entreat her show a woman’s pity.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: What, wouldst thou have me prove myself a bastard?

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: ’Tis true the raven doth not hatch a lark.

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: Yet have I heard—O, could I find it now!—

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: The lion, moved with pity, did endure

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: To have his princely paws pared all away.

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: Some say that ravens foster forlorn children,

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: The whilst their own birds famish in their nests.

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: O, be to me, though thy hard heart say no,

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: Nothing so kind, but something pitiful.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: I know not what it means; away with her!

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: O, let me teach thee! For my father’s sake,

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: That gave thee life when well he might have slain thee,

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: Be not obdurate, open thy deaf ears.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Hadst thou in person ne’er offended me,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Even for his sake am I pitiless.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Remember, boys, I poured forth tears in vain

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: To save your brother from the sacrifice,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: But fierce Andronicus would not relent.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Therefore away with her, and use her as you will;

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: The worse to her, the better loved of me.

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: O Tamora, be called a gentle queen,

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: And with thine own hands kill me in this place!

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: For ’tis not life that I have begged so long;

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: Poor I was slain when Bassianus died.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: What begg’st thou, then? Fond woman, let me go.

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: ’Tis present death I beg; and one thing more

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: That womanhood denies my tongue to tell.

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: O, keep me from their worse than killing lust,

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: And tumble me into some loathsome pit,

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: Where never man’s eye may behold my body.

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: Do this, and be a charitable murderer.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: So should I rob my sweet sons of their fee.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: No, let them satisfy their lust on thee.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Away, for thou hast stayed us here too long.

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: No grace, no womanhood? Ah, beastly creature,

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: The blot and enemy to our general name!

lines.speaker: LAVINIA
lines.text: Confusion fall—

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: Nay, then I’ll stop your mouth. Bring thou her husband.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: This is the hole where Aaron bid us hide him.
[_They put Bassianus’s body in the pit and exit, carrying off Lavinia._]

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Farewell, my sons. See that you make her sure.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Ne’er let my heart know merry cheer indeed

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Till all the Andronici be made away.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Now will I hence to seek my lovely Moor,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And let my spleenful sons this trull deflower.
[_Exit._]
Enter Aaron with two of Titus’ sons, Quintus and Martius.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Come on, my lords, the better foot before.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Straight will I bring you to the loathsome pit

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Where I espied the panther fast asleep.

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: My sight is very dull, whate’er it bodes.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: And mine, I promise you. Were it not for shame,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Well could I leave our sport to sleep awhile.
[_He falls into the pit._]

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: What, art thou fallen? What subtle hole is this,

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: Whose mouth is covered with rude-growing briers,

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: Upon whose leaves are drops of new-shed blood

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: As fresh as morning dew distilled on flowers?

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: A very fatal place it seems to me.

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: Speak, brother, hast thou hurt thee with the fall?

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: O brother, with the dismall’st object hurt

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: That ever eye with sight made heart lament!
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Now will I fetch the king to find them here,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: That he thereby may have a likely guess

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: How these were they that made away his brother.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Why dost not comfort me, and help me out

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: From this unhallowed and blood-stained hole?

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: I am surprised with an uncouth fear;

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: A chilling sweat o’er-runs my trembling joints.

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: My heart suspects more than mine eye can see.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: To prove thou hast a true-divining heart,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Aaron and thou look down into this den,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: And see a fearful sight of blood and death.

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: Aaron is gone, and my compassionate heart

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: Will not permit mine eyes once to behold

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: The thing whereat it trembles by surmise.

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: O, tell me who it is; for ne’er till now

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: Was I a child to fear I know not what.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Lord Bassianus lies berayed in blood,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: All on a heap, like to a slaughtered lamb,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: In this detested, dark, blood-drinking pit.

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: If it be dark, how dost thou know ’tis he?

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Upon his bloody finger he doth wear

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: A precious ring that lightens all the hole,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Which, like a taper in some monument,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Doth shine upon the dead man’s earthy cheeks,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: And shows the ragged entrails of the pit.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: So pale did shine the moon on Pyramus

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: When he by night lay bathed in maiden blood.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: O brother, help me with thy fainting hand,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: If fear hath made thee faint, as me it hath,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Out of this fell devouring receptacle,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: As hateful as Cocytus’ misty mouth.

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: Reach me thy hand, that I may help thee out,

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: Or, wanting strength to do thee so much good,

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: I may be plucked into the swallowing womb

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: Of this deep pit, poor Bassianus’ grave.

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: I have no strength to pluck thee to the brink.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Nor I no strength to climb without thy help.

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: Thy hand once more; I will not loose again,

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: Till thou art here aloft, or I below.

lines.speaker: QUINTUS
lines.text: Thou canst not come to me. I come to thee.
[_Falls in._]
Enter the Emperor Saturninus and Aaron the Moor.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Along with me! I’ll see what hole is here,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: And what he is that now is leapt into it.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Say, who art thou that lately didst descend

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Into this gaping hollow of the earth?

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: The unhappy sons of old Andronicus,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Brought hither in a most unlucky hour,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: To find thy brother Bassianus dead.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: My brother dead! I know thou dost but jest.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: He and his lady both are at the lodge

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Upon the north side of this pleasant chase;

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: ’Tis not an hour since I left them there.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: We know not where you left them all alive;

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: But, out, alas, here have we found him dead.
Enter Tamora, Titus Andronicus and Lucius.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Where is my lord the king?

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Here, Tamora; though grieved with killing grief.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Where is thy brother Bassianus?

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Now to the bottom dost thou search my wound.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Poor Bassianus here lies murdered.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Then all too late I bring this fatal writ,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: The complot of this timeless tragedy;

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And wonder greatly that man’s face can fold

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: In pleasing smiles such murderous tyranny.
[_She giveth Saturnine a letter._]
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: _An if we miss to meet him handsomely,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Sweet huntsman, Bassianus ’tis we mean,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Do thou so much as dig the grave for him;

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Thou know’st our meaning. Look for thy reward

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Among the nettles at the elder-tree

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Which overshades the mouth of that same pit

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Where we decreed to bury Bassianus.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Do this, and purchase us thy lasting friends._

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: O Tamora, was ever heard the like?

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: This is the pit, and this the elder-tree.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Look, sirs, if you can find the huntsman out

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: That should have murdered Bassianus here.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: My gracious lord, here is the bag of gold.
[_Showing it._]
[_To Titus_.]

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Two of thy whelps, fell curs of bloody kind,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Have here bereft my brother of his life.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Sirs, drag them from the pit unto the prison.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: There let them bide until we have devised

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Some never-heard-of torturing pain for them.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: What, are they in this pit? O wondrous thing!

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: How easily murder is discovered!

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: High emperor, upon my feeble knee

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: I beg this boon, with tears not lightly shed,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: That this fell fault of my accursed sons,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Accursed if the fault be proved in them—

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: If it be proved! You see it is apparent.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Who found this letter? Tamora, was it you?

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Andronicus himself did take it up.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: I did, my lord, yet let me be their bail;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: For by my fathers’ reverend tomb I vow

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: They shall be ready at your highness’ will

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: To answer their suspicion with their lives.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Thou shalt not bail them. See thou follow me.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Some bring the murdered body, some the murderers.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Let them not speak a word; the guilt is plain;

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: For, by my soul, were there worse end than death,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: That end upon them should be executed.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Andronicus, I will entreat the king.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Fear not thy sons; they shall do well enough.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Come, Lucius, come; stay not to talk with them.
[_Exeunt severally. Attendants bearing the body._]
Enter the empress’ sons, Demetrius and Chiron with Lavinia, her hands cut off, and her tongue cut out, and ravished.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: So, now go tell, an if thy tongue can speak,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Who ’twas that cut thy tongue and ravished thee.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: Write down thy mind, bewray thy meaning so,

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: An if thy stumps will let thee play the scribe.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: See how with signs and tokens she can scrowl.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: Go home, call for sweet water, wash thy hands.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: She hath no tongue to call, nor hands to wash;

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: And so let’s leave her to her silent walks.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: An ’twere my cause, I should go hang myself.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: If thou hadst hands to help thee knit the cord.
[_Exeunt Chiron and Demetrius._]
Enter Marcus, from hunting.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Who is this? My niece, that flies away so fast?

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Cousin, a word; where is your husband?

lines.speaker: MARCUS
