lines.text: If I do dream, would all my wealth would wake me!

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: If I do wake, some planet strike me down,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: That I may slumber an eternal sleep!

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Speak, gentle niece, what stern ungentle hands

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Hath lopped and hewed and made thy body bare

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Of her two branches, those sweet ornaments

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Whose circling shadows kings have sought to sleep in,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And might not gain so great a happiness

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: As half thy love? Why dost not speak to me?

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Alas, a crimson river of warm blood,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Like to a bubbling fountain stirred with wind,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Doth rise and fall between thy rosed lips,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Coming and going with thy honey breath.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: But sure some Tereus hath deflowered thee,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And, lest thou shouldst detect him, cut thy tongue.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Ah, now thou turn’st away thy face for shame,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And notwithstanding all this loss of blood,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: As from a conduit with three issuing spouts,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Yet do thy cheeks look red as Titan’s face

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Blushing to be encountered with a cloud.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Shall I speak for thee, shall I say ’tis so?

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: O, that I knew thy heart, and knew the beast,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: That I might rail at him to ease my mind.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Sorrow concealed, like an oven stopped,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Doth burn the heart to cinders where it is.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Fair Philomela, why she but lost her tongue,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And in a tedious sampler sewed her mind;

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: But, lovely niece, that mean is cut from thee;

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: A craftier Tereus, cousin, hast thou met,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And he hath cut those pretty fingers off

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: That could have better sewed than Philomel.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: O, had the monster seen those lily hands

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Tremble like aspen leaves upon a lute,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And make the silken strings delight to kiss them,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: He would not then have touched them for his life.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Or had he heard the heavenly harmony

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Which that sweet tongue hath made,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: He would have dropped his knife, and fell asleep,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: As Cerberus at the Thracian poet’s feet.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Come, let us go, and make thy father blind,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: For such a sight will blind a father’s eye.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: One hour’s storm will drown the fragrant meads;

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: What will whole months of tears thy father’s eyes?

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Do not draw back, for we will mourn with thee.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: O, could our mourning ease thy misery!
[_Exeunt._]
Enter the Judges and Senators, with Titus’ two sons Quintus and Martius bound, passing on the stage to the place of execution, and Titus going before, pleading.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Hear me, grave fathers; noble tribunes, stay!

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: For pity of mine age, whose youth was spent

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: In dangerous wars whilst you securely slept;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: For all my blood in Rome’s great quarrel shed,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: For all the frosty nights that I have watched,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And for these bitter tears, which now you see

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Filling the aged wrinkles in my cheeks,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Be pitiful to my condemned sons,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Whose souls are not corrupted as ’tis thought.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: For two and twenty sons I never wept,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Because they died in honour’s lofty bed.
[_Andronicus lieth down, and the Judges pass by him._]
[_Exeunt with the prisoners as Titus continues speaking._]

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: For these, tribunes, in the dust I write

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: My heart’s deep languor and my soul’s sad tears.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Let my tears staunch the earth’s dry appetite;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: My sons’ sweet blood will make it shame and blush.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: O earth, I will befriend thee more with rain

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: That shall distil from these two ancient urns,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Than youthful April shall with all his showers.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: In summer’s drought I’ll drop upon thee still;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: In winter with warm tears I’ll melt the snow,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And keep eternal spring-time on thy face,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: So thou refuse to drink my dear sons’ blood.
Enter Lucius with his weapon drawn.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: O reverend tribunes! O gentle aged men!

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Unbind my sons, reverse the doom of death;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And let me say, that never wept before,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: My tears are now prevailing orators.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: O noble father, you lament in vain.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: The tribunes hear you not, no man is by;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And you recount your sorrows to a stone.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Ah, Lucius, for thy brothers let me plead.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Grave tribunes, once more I entreat of you—

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: My gracious lord, no tribune hears you speak.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Why, ’tis no matter, man. If they did hear,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: They would not mark me; if they did mark,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: They would not pity me, yet plead I must,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And bootless unto them.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Therefore I tell my sorrows to the stones,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Who, though they cannot answer my distress,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Yet in some sort they are better than the tribunes,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: For that they will not intercept my tale.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: When I do weep, they humbly at my feet

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Receive my tears, and seem to weep with me;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And were they but attired in grave weeds,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Rome could afford no tribunes like to these.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: A stone is soft as wax, tribunes more hard than stones;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: A stone is silent, and offendeth not,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And tribunes with their tongues doom men to death.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: But wherefore stand’st thou with thy weapon drawn?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: To rescue my two brothers from their death;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: For which attempt the judges have pronounced

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: My everlasting doom of banishment.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: O happy man, they have befriended thee.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Why, foolish Lucius, dost thou not perceive

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: That Rome is but a wilderness of tigers?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Tigers must prey, and Rome affords no prey

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: But me and mine. How happy art thou then,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: From these devourers to be banished!

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: But who comes with our brother Marcus here?
Enter Marcus with Lavinia.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Titus, prepare thy aged eyes to weep;

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Or if not so, thy noble heart to break.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: I bring consuming sorrow to thine age.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Will it consume me? Let me see it then.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: This was thy daughter.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Why, Marcus, so she is.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Ay me, this object kills me!

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Faint-hearted boy, arise, and look upon her.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Speak, Lavinia, what accursed hand

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Hath made thee handless in thy father’s sight?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: What fool hath added water to the sea,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Or brought a faggot to bright-burning Troy?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: My grief was at the height before thou cam’st,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And now like Nilus it disdaineth bounds.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Give me a sword, I’ll chop off my hands too;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: For they have fought for Rome, and all in vain;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And they have nursed this woe in feeding life;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: In bootless prayer have they been held up,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And they have served me to effectless use.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Now all the service I require of them

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Is that the one will help to cut the other.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: ’Tis well, Lavinia, that thou hast no hands,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: For hands to do Rome service is but vain.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Speak, gentle sister, who hath martyred thee?

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: O, that delightful engine of her thoughts,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: That blabbed them with such pleasing eloquence,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Is torn from forth that pretty hollow cage,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Where, like a sweet melodious bird, it sung

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Sweet varied notes, enchanting every ear.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: O, say thou for her, who hath done this deed?

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: O, thus I found her straying in the park,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Seeking to hide herself, as doth the deer

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: That hath received some unrecuring wound.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: It was my dear, and he that wounded her

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Hath hurt me more than had he killed me dead.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: For now I stand as one upon a rock,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Environed with a wilderness of sea,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Who marks the waxing tide grow wave by wave,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Expecting ever when some envious surge

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Will in his brinish bowels swallow him.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: This way to death my wretched sons are gone;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Here stands my other son, a banished man,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And here my brother, weeping at my woes.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: But that which gives my soul the greatest spurn

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Is dear Lavinia, dearer than my soul.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Had I but seen thy picture in this plight

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: It would have madded me. What shall I do

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Now I behold thy lively body so?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Thou hast no hands to wipe away thy tears,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Nor tongue to tell me who hath martyred thee.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Thy husband he is dead, and for his death

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Thy brothers are condemned, and dead by this.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Look, Marcus! Ah, son Lucius, look on her!

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: When I did name her brothers, then fresh tears

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Stood on her cheeks, as doth the honey-dew

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Upon a gathered lily almost withered.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Perchance she weeps because they killed her husband;

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Perchance because she knows them innocent.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: If they did kill thy husband, then be joyful,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Because the law hath ta’en revenge on them.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: No, no, they would not do so foul a deed;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Witness the sorrow that their sister makes.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Gentle Lavinia, let me kiss thy lips,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Or make some sign how I may do thee ease.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Shall thy good uncle, and thy brother Lucius,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And thou, and I, sit round about some fountain,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Looking all downwards to behold our cheeks

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: How they are stained, like meadows yet not dry,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: With miry slime left on them by a flood?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And in the fountain shall we gaze so long

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Till the fresh taste be taken from that clearness,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And made a brine-pit with our bitter tears?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Or shall we cut away our hands like thine?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Or shall we bite our tongues, and in dumb shows

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Pass the remainder of our hateful days?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: What shall we do? Let us that have our tongues

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Plot some device of further misery,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: To make us wondered at in time to come.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Sweet father, cease your tears; for at your grief

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: See how my wretched sister sobs and weeps.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Patience, dear niece. Good Titus, dry thine eyes.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Ah, Marcus, Marcus! Brother, well I wot

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Thy napkin cannot drink a tear of mine,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: For thou, poor man, hast drowned it with thine own.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Ah, my Lavinia, I will wipe thy cheeks.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Mark, Marcus, mark! I understand her signs.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Had she a tongue to speak, now would she say

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: That to her brother which I said to thee.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: His napkin, with his true tears all bewet,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Can do no service on her sorrowful cheeks.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: O, what a sympathy of woe is this,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: As far from help as limbo is from bliss.
Enter Aaron the Moor, alone.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Titus Andronicus, my lord the emperor

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Sends thee this word, that, if thou love thy sons,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Let Marcus, Lucius, or thyself, old Titus,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Or any one of you, chop off your hand

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And send it to the king; he for the same

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Will send thee hither both thy sons alive,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And that shall be the ransom for their fault.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: O gracious emperor! O gentle Aaron!

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Did ever raven sing so like a lark

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: That gives sweet tidings of the sun’s uprise?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: With all my heart I’ll send the emperor my hand.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Good Aaron, wilt thou help to chop it off?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Stay, father, for that noble hand of thine,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: That hath thrown down so many enemies,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Shall not be sent. My hand will serve the turn.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: My youth can better spare my blood than you;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And therefore mine shall save my brothers’ lives.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Which of your hands hath not defended Rome,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And reared aloft the bloody battle-axe,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Writing destruction on the enemy’s castle?

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: O, none of both but are of high desert.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: My hand hath been but idle; let it serve

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: To ransom my two nephews from their death;

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Then have I kept it to a worthy end.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Nay, come, agree whose hand shall go along,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: For fear they die before their pardon come.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: My hand shall go.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: By heaven, it shall not go!

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Sirs, strive no more. Such withered herbs as these

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Are meet for plucking up, and therefore mine.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Sweet father, if I shall be thought thy son,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Let me redeem my brothers both from death.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And for our father’s sake and mother’s care,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Now let me show a brother’s love to thee.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Agree between you; I will spare my hand.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Then I’ll go fetch an axe.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: But I will use the axe.
[_Exeunt Lucius and Marcus._]

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Come hither, Aaron; I’ll deceive them both.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Lend me thy hand, and I will give thee mine.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: If that be called deceit, I will be honest,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And never whilst I live deceive men so.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: But I’ll deceive you in another sort,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And that you’ll say ere half an hour pass.
[_He cuts off Titus’s hand._]
Enter Lucius and Marcus again.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Now stay your strife. What shall be is dispatched.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Good Aaron, give his majesty my hand.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Tell him it was a hand that warded him

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: From thousand dangers, bid him bury it;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: More hath it merited, that let it have.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: As for my sons, say I account of them

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: As jewels purchased at an easy price;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And yet dear too, because I bought mine own.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: I go, Andronicus; and for thy hand

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Look by and by to have thy sons with thee.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Their heads, I mean. O, how this villainy

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Doth fat me with the very thoughts of it!

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Let fools do good, and fair men call for grace,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Aaron will have his soul black like his face.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: O, here I lift this one hand up to heaven,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And bow this feeble ruin to the earth.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: If any power pities wretched tears,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: To that I call! [_To Lavinia_.] What, wouldst thou kneel with me?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Do, then, dear heart; for heaven shall hear our prayers,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Or with our sighs we’ll breathe the welkin dim,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And stain the sun with fog, as sometime clouds

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: When they do hug him in their melting bosoms.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: O brother, speak with possibility,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And do not break into these deep extremes.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Is not my sorrow deep, having no bottom?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Then be my passions bottomless with them.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: But yet let reason govern thy lament.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: If there were reason for these miseries,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Then into limits could I bind my woes.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: When heaven doth weep, doth not the earth o’erflow?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: If the winds rage, doth not the sea wax mad,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Threatening the welkin with his big-swol’n face?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And wilt thou have a reason for this coil?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: I am the sea. Hark how her sighs doth flow!

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: She is the weeping welkin, I the earth.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Then must my sea be moved with her sighs;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Then must my earth with her continual tears

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Become a deluge, overflowed and drowned;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: For why my bowels cannot hide her woes,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: But like a drunkard must I vomit them.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Then give me leave, for losers will have leave

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: To ease their stomachs with their bitter tongues.
Enter a Messenger with two heads and a hand.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Worthy Andronicus, ill art thou repaid

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: For that good hand thou sent’st the emperor.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Here are the heads of thy two noble sons,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And here’s thy hand, in scorn to thee sent back.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Thy grief their sports, thy resolution mocked;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: That woe is me to think upon thy woes,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: More than remembrance of my father’s death.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Now let hot Etna cool in Sicily,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And be my heart an ever-burning hell!

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: These miseries are more than may be borne.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: To weep with them that weep doth ease some deal,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: But sorrow flouted at is double death.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Ah, that this sight should make so deep a wound,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And yet detested life not shrink thereat!

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: That ever death should let life bear his name,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Where life hath no more interest but to breathe!
[_Lavinia kisses Titus._]

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Alas, poor heart, that kiss is comfortless

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: As frozen water to a starved snake.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: When will this fearful slumber have an end?

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Now farewell, flattery; die, Andronicus;

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Thou dost not slumber. See thy two sons’ heads,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Thy warlike hand, thy mangled daughter here;

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Thy other banished son with this dear sight

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Struck pale and bloodless; and thy brother, I,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Even like a stony image, cold and numb.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Ah, now no more will I control thy griefs.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Rent off thy silver hair, thy other hand

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Gnawing with thy teeth; and be this dismal sight

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: The closing up of our most wretched eyes.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Now is a time to storm; why art thou still?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Ha, ha, ha!

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Why dost thou laugh? It fits not with this hour.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Why, I have not another tear to shed.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Besides, this sorrow is an enemy,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And would usurp upon my watery eyes,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And make them blind with tributary tears.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Then which way shall I find Revenge’s cave?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: For these two heads do seem to speak to me,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And threat me I shall never come to bliss

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Till all these mischiefs be returned again

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Even in their throats that have committed them.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Come, let me see what task I have to do.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: You heavy people, circle me about,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: That I may turn me to each one of you,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And swear unto my soul to right your wrongs.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: The vow is made. Come, brother, take a head;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And in this hand the other will I bear.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And, Lavinia, thou shalt be employed in these arms.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Bear thou my hand, sweet wench, between thy teeth.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: As for thee, boy, go, get thee from my sight;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Thou art an exile, and thou must not stay.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Hie to the Goths, and raise an army there.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And if you love me, as I think you do,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Let’s kiss and part, for we have much to do.
[_Exeunt Titus, Marcus and Lavinia._]

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Farewell, Andronicus, my noble father,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: The woefull’st man that ever lived in Rome.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Farewell, proud Rome, till Lucius come again;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: He loves his pledges dearer than his life.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Farewell, Lavinia, my noble sister;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: O, would thou wert as thou tofore hast been!

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: But now nor Lucius nor Lavinia lives

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: But in oblivion and hateful griefs.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: If Lucius live, he will requite your wrongs,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And make proud Saturnine and his empress

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Beg at the gates, like Tarquin and his queen.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Now will I to the Goths, and raise a power

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: To be revenged on Rome and Saturnine.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Rome. A Room in Titus’s House. A banquet set out

lines.text: Enter Titus Andronicus, Marcus, Lavinia and the boy Young Lucius.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: So so; now sit; and look you eat no more

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Than will preserve just so much strength in us

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: As will revenge these bitter woes of ours.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Marcus, unknit that sorrow-wreathen knot.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Thy niece and I, poor creatures, want our hands,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And cannot passionate our tenfold grief

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: With folded arms. This poor right hand of mine

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Is left to tyrannize upon my breast;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Who when my heart, all mad with misery,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Beats in this hollow prison of my flesh,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Then thus I thump it down.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Thou map of woe, that thus dost talk in signs,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: When thy poor heart beats with outrageous beating,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Thou canst not strike it thus to make it still.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Wound it with sighing, girl, kill it with groans;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Or get some little knife between thy teeth,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And just against thy heart make thou a hole,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: That all the tears that thy poor eyes let fall

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: May run into that sink, and, soaking in,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Drown the lamenting fool in sea-salt tears.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Fie, brother, fie! Teach her not thus to lay

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Such violent hands upon her tender life.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: How now! Has sorrow made thee dote already?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Why, Marcus, no man should be mad but I.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: What violent hands can she lay on her life?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Ah, wherefore dost thou urge the name of hands,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: To bid Æneas tell the tale twice o’er

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: How Troy was burnt and he made miserable?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: O, handle not the theme, to talk of hands,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Lest we remember still that we have none.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Fie, fie, how frantically I square my talk,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: As if we should forget we had no hands,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: If Marcus did not name the word of hands!

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Come, let’s fall to; and, gentle girl, eat this.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Here is no drink! Hark, Marcus, what she says;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: I can interpret all her martyred signs.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: She says she drinks no other drink but tears,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Brewed with her sorrow, meshed upon her cheeks.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Speechless complainer, I will learn thy thought;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: In thy dumb action will I be as perfect

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: As begging hermits in their holy prayers.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Thou shalt not sigh, nor hold thy stumps to heaven,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Nor wink, nor nod, nor kneel, nor make a sign,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: But I of these will wrest an alphabet,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And by still practice learn to know thy meaning.

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: Good grandsire, leave these bitter deep laments.

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: Make my aunt merry with some pleasing tale.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Alas, the tender boy, in passion moved,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Doth weep to see his grandsire’s heaviness.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Peace, tender sapling; thou art made of tears,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And tears will quickly melt thy life away.
[_Marcus strikes the dish with a knife._]

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: What dost thou strike at, Marcus, with thy knife?

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: At that that I have killed, my lord, a fly.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Out on thee, murderer! Thou kill’st my heart;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Mine eyes are cloyed with view of tyranny;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: A deed of death done on the innocent

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Becomes not Titus’ brother. Get thee gone;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: I see thou art not for my company.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Alas, my lord, I have but killed a fly.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: “But”? How if that fly had a father and mother?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: How would he hang his slender gilded wings

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And buzz lamenting doings in the air!

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Poor harmless fly,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: That with his pretty buzzing melody,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Came here to make us merry, and thou hast killed him.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Pardon me, sir; ’twas a black ill-favoured fly,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Like to the empress’ Moor; therefore I killed him.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: O, O, O!

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Then pardon me for reprehending thee,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: For thou hast done a charitable deed.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Give me thy knife, I will insult on him,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Flattering myself as if it were the Moor

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Come hither purposely to poison me.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: There’s for thyself, and that’s for Tamora.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Ah, sirrah!

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Yet, I think, we are not brought so low

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: But that between us we can kill a fly

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: That comes in likeness of a coal-black Moor.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Alas, poor man, grief has so wrought on him,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: He takes false shadows for true substances.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Come, take away. Lavinia, go with me.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: I’ll to thy closet, and go read with thee

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Sad stories chanced in the times of old.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Come, boy, and go with me. Thy sight is young,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And thou shalt read when mine begin to dazzle.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Young Lucius and Lavinia running after him, and the boy flies from her with his books under his arm. Enter Titus and Marcus.

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: Help, grandsire, help! My aunt Lavinia

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: Follows me everywhere, I know not why.

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: Good uncle Marcus, see how swift she comes!

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: Alas, sweet aunt, I know not what you mean.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Stand by me, Lucius. Do not fear thine aunt.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: She loves thee, boy, too well to do thee harm.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: YOUNG LUCIUS

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Ay, when my father was in Rome she did.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: What means my niece Lavinia by these signs?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Fear her not, Lucius. Somewhat doth she mean.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: See, Lucius, see how much she makes of thee.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Somewhither would she have thee go with her.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Ah, boy, Cornelia never with more care

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Read to her sons than she hath read to thee

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Sweet poetry and Tully’s _Orator_.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Canst thou not guess wherefore she plies thee thus?

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: My lord, I know not, I, nor can I guess,

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: Unless some fit or frenzy do possess her;

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: For I have heard my grandsire say full oft,

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: Extremity of griefs would make men mad;

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: And I have read that Hecuba of Troy

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: Ran mad for sorrow. That made me to fear,

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: Although, my lord, I know my noble aunt

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: Loves me as dear as e’er my mother did,

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: And would not, but in fury, fright my youth;

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: Which made me down to throw my books, and fly,

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: Causeless, perhaps. But pardon me, sweet aunt.

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: And, madam, if my uncle Marcus go,

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: I will most willingly attend your ladyship.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Lucius, I will.
[_Lavinia turns over with her stumps the books which Lucius has let fall._]

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: How now, Lavinia? Marcus, what means this?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Some book there is that she desires to see.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Which is it, girl, of these? Open them, boy.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: But thou art deeper read and better skilled.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Come and take choice of all my library,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And so beguile thy sorrow, till the heavens

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Reveal the damned contriver of this deed.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Why lifts she up her arms in sequence thus?

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: I think she means that there were more than one

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Confederate in the fact. Ay, more there was,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Or else to heaven she heaves them for revenge.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Lucius, what book is that she tosseth so?

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: Grandsire, ’tis Ovid’s _Metamorphosis_.

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: My mother gave it me.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: For love of her that’s gone,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Perhaps, she culled it from among the rest.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Soft! So busily she turns the leaves!

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Help her! What would she find? Lavinia, shall I read?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: This is the tragic tale of Philomel,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And treats of Tereus’ treason and his rape;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And rape, I fear, was root of thy annoy.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: See, brother, see! Note how she quotes the leaves.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Lavinia, wert thou thus surprised, sweet girl,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Ravished and wronged, as Philomela was,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Forced in the ruthless, vast, and gloomy woods?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: See, see!

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Ay, such a place there is where we did hunt,—

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: O, had we never, never hunted there!—

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Patterned by that the poet here describes,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: By nature made for murders and for rapes.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: O, why should nature build so foul a den,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Unless the gods delight in tragedies?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Give signs, sweet girl, for here are none but friends,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: What Roman lord it was durst do the deed.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Or slunk not Saturnine, as Tarquin erst,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: That left the camp to sin in Lucrece’ bed?

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Sit down, sweet niece. Brother, sit down by me.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Apollo, Pallas, Jove, or Mercury,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Inspire me, that I may this treason find!

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: My lord, look here. Look here, Lavinia.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: This sandy plot is plain; guide, if thou canst,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: This after me. I have writ my name
[_He writes his name with his staff and guides it with feet and mouth._]

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Without the help of any hand at all.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Cursed be that heart that forced us to this shift!

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Write thou, good niece, and here display at last

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: What God will have discovered for revenge.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Heaven guide thy pen to print thy sorrows plain,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: That we may know the traitors and the truth!
[_She takes the staff in her mouth, and guides it with her stumps and writes._]

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: O, do ye read, my lord, what she hath writ?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: “_Stuprum_. Chiron. Demetrius.”

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: What, what! The lustful sons of Tamora

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Performers of this heinous bloody deed?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: _Magni Dominator poli,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Tam lentus audis scelera, tam lentus vides?_

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: O, calm thee, gentle lord, although I know

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: There is enough written upon this earth

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: To stir a mutiny in the mildest thoughts

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And arm the minds of infants to exclaims.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: My lord, kneel down with me; Lavinia, kneel;

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And kneel, sweet boy, the Roman Hector’s hope;

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And swear with me, as, with the woeful fere

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And father of that chaste dishonoured dame,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Lord Junius Brutus sware for Lucrece’ rape,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: That we will prosecute, by good advice

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Mortal revenge upon these traitorous Goths,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And see their blood, or die with this reproach.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: ’Tis sure enough, an you knew how.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: But if you hunt these bear-whelps, then beware;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: The dam will wake, and if she wind you once.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: She’s with the lion deeply still in league,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And lulls him whilst she playeth on her back,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And when he sleeps will she do what she list.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: You are a young huntsman, Marcus; let alone;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And come, I will go get a leaf of brass,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And with a gad of steel will write these words,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And lay it by. The angry northern wind

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Will blow these sands like Sibyl’s leaves abroad,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And where’s our lesson, then? Boy, what say you?

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: I say, my lord, that if I were a man,

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: Their mother’s bedchamber should not be safe

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: For these base bondmen to the yoke of Rome.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Ay, that’s my boy! Thy father hath full oft

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: For his ungrateful country done the like.

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: And, uncle, so will I, an if I live.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Come, go with me into mine armoury.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Lucius, I’ll fit thee; and withal, my boy,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Shall carry from me to the empress’ sons

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Presents that I intend to send them both.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Come, come; thou’lt do my message, wilt thou not?

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: Ay, with my dagger in their bosoms, grandsire.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: No, boy, not so. I’ll teach thee another course.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Lavinia, come. Marcus, look to my house.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Lucius and I’ll go brave it at the court;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Ay, marry, will we, sir; and we’ll be waited on.
[_Exeunt Titus, Lavinia and Young Lucius._]

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: O heavens, can you hear a good man groan

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And not relent, or not compassion him?

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Marcus, attend him in his ecstasy,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: That hath more scars of sorrow in his heart

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Than foemen’s marks upon his battered shield,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: But yet so just that he will not revenge.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Revenge ye heavens for old Andronicus!
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Rome. A Room in the Palace

lines.text: Enter Aaron, Chiron and Demetrius at one door, and at the other door Young Lucius and another, with a bundle of weapons and verses writ upon them.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: Demetrius, here’s the son of Lucius;

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: He hath some message to deliver us.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Ay, some mad message from his mad grandfather.

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: My lords, with all the humbleness I may,

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: I greet your honours from Andronicus;
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: And pray the Roman gods confound you both.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Gramercy, lovely Lucius. What’s the news?
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: That you are both deciphered, that’s the news,

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: For villains marked with rape. [_Aloud_.] May it please you,

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: My grandsire, well advised, hath sent by me

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: The goodliest weapons of his armoury

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: To gratify your honourable youth,

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: The hope of Rome; for so he bid me say;

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: And so I do, and with his gifts present

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: Your lordships, that, whenever you have need,

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: You may be armed and appointed well.

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: And so I leave you both, [_Aside_.] like bloody villains.
[_Exeunt Young Lucius and Attendant._]

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: What’s here? A scroll; and written round about?

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Let’s see:
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: _Integer vitae, scelerisque purus,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Non eget Mauri iaculis, nec arcu._

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: O, ’tis a verse in Horace; I know it well.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: I read it in the grammar long ago.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Ay, just; a verse in Horace; right, you have it.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Now, what a thing it is to be an ass!

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Here’s no sound jest! The old man hath found their guilt,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And sends them weapons wrapped about with lines,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: That wound, beyond their feeling, to the quick.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: But were our witty empress well afoot,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: She would applaud Andronicus’ conceit.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: But let her rest in her unrest awhile.—

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And now, young lords, was’t not a happy star

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Led us to Rome, strangers, and more than so,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Captives, to be advanced to this height?

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: It did me good before the palace gate

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: To brave the tribune in his brother’s hearing.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: But me more good to see so great a lord

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Basely insinuate and send us gifts.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Had he not reason, Lord Demetrius?

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Did you not use his daughter very friendly?

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: I would we had a thousand Roman dames

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: At such a bay, by turn to serve our lust.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: A charitable wish, and full of love.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Here lacks but your mother for to say amen.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: And that would she for twenty thousand more.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Come, let us go and pray to all the gods

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: For our beloved mother in her pains.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Pray to the devils; the gods have given us over.
[_Trumpets sound._]

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Why do the emperor’s trumpets flourish thus?

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: Belike for joy the emperor hath a son.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Soft, who comes here?
Enter Nurse with a blackamoor Child in her arms.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Good morrow, lords.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: O, tell me, did you see Aaron the Moor?

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Well, more or less, or ne’er a whit at all,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Here Aaron is; and what with Aaron now?

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: O gentle Aaron, we are all undone!

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Now help, or woe betide thee evermore!

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Why, what a caterwauling dost thou keep!

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: What dost thou wrap and fumble in thy arms?

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: O, that which I would hide from heaven’s eye,

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Our empress’ shame and stately Rome’s disgrace.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: She is delivered, lords, she is delivered.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: To whom?

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: I mean, she’s brought a-bed.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Well, God give her good rest! What hath he sent her?

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: A devil.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Why, then she is the devil’s dam. A joyful issue.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: A joyless, dismal, black, and sorrowful issue.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Here is the babe, as loathsome as a toad

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Amongst the fair-faced breeders of our clime.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: The empress sends it thee, thy stamp, thy seal,

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: And bids thee christen it with thy dagger’s point.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Zounds, ye whore, is black so base a hue?

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Sweet blowse, you are a beauteous blossom sure.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Villain, what hast thou done?

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: That which thou canst not undo.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: Thou hast undone our mother.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Villain, I have done thy mother.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: And therein, hellish dog, thou hast undone her.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Woe to her chance, and damned her loathed choice!

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Accursed the offspring of so foul a fiend!

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: It shall not live.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: It shall not die.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Aaron, it must; the mother wills it so.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: What, must it, nurse? Then let no man but I

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Do execution on my flesh and blood.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: I’ll broach the tadpole on my rapier’s point.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Nurse, give it me; my sword shall soon dispatch it.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Sooner this sword shall plough thy bowels up.
[_Taking the baby._]

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Stay, murderous villains, will you kill your brother?

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Now, by the burning tapers of the sky

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: That shone so brightly when this boy was got,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: He dies upon my scimitar’s sharp point

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: That touches this my first-born son and heir.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: I tell you, younglings, not Enceladus,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: With all his threatening band of Typhon’s brood,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Nor great Alcides, nor the god of war,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Shall seize this prey out of his father’s hands.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: What, what, ye sanguine, shallow-hearted boys!

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Ye white-limed walls, ye alehouse-painted signs!

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Coal-black is better than another hue

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: In that it scorns to bear another hue;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: For all the water in the ocean

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Can never turn the swan’s black legs to white,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Although she lave them hourly in the flood.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Tell the empress from me, I am of age

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: To keep mine own, excuse it how she can.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Wilt thou betray thy noble mistress thus?

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: My mistress is my mistress; this my self;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: The vigour and the picture of my youth.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: This before all the world do I prefer;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: This maugre all the world will I keep safe,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Or some of you shall smoke for it in Rome.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: By this our mother is for ever shamed.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: Rome will despise her for this foul escape.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: The emperor in his rage will doom her death.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: I blush to think upon this ignomy.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Why, there’s the privilege your beauty bears.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Fie, treacherous hue, that will betray with blushing

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: The close enacts and counsels of thy heart!

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Here’s a young lad framed of another leer.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Look how the black slave smiles upon the father,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: As who should say “Old lad, I am thine own.”

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: He is your brother, lords, sensibly fed

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Of that self blood that first gave life to you;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And from your womb where you imprisoned were

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: He is enfranchised and come to light.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Nay, he is your brother by the surer side,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Although my seal be stamped in his face.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Aaron, what shall I say unto the empress?

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Advise thee, Aaron, what is to be done,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: And we will all subscribe to thy advice.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Save thou the child, so we may all be safe.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Then sit we down, and let us all consult.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: My son and I will have the wind of you.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Keep there. Now talk at pleasure of your safety.
[_They sit._]

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: How many women saw this child of his?

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Why, so, brave lords! When we join in league,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: I am a lamb; but if you brave the Moor,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: The chafed boar, the mountain lioness,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: The ocean swells not so as Aaron storms.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: But say again, how many saw the child?

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Cornelia the midwife and myself,

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: And no one else but the delivered empress.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: The empress, the midwife, and yourself.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Two may keep counsel when the third’s away.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Go to the empress; tell her this I said.
[_He kills her._]

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: “Wheak, wheak!” So cries a pig prepared to the spit.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: What mean’st thou, Aaron? Wherefore didst thou this?

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: O Lord, sir, ’tis a deed of policy.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Shall she live to betray this guilt of ours,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: A long-tongued babbling gossip? No, lords, no.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And now be it known to you my full intent.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Not far, one Muliteus lives, my countryman;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: His wife but yesternight was brought to bed.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: His child is like to her, fair as you are.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Go pack with him, and give the mother gold,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And tell them both the circumstance of all,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And how by this their child shall be advanced,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And be received for the emperor’s heir,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And substituted in the place of mine,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: To calm this tempest whirling in the court;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And let the emperor dandle him for his own.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Hark ye, lords; ye see I have given her physic,
[_Indicating the Nurse._]

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And you must needs bestow her funeral;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: The fields are near, and you are gallant grooms.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: This done, see that you take no longer days,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: But send the midwife presently to me.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: The midwife and the nurse well made away,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Then let the ladies tattle what they please.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: Aaron, I see thou wilt not trust the air

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: With secrets.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: For this care of Tamora,

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Herself and hers are highly bound to thee.
[_Exeunt Demetrius and Chiron, carrying the Nurse’s body._]

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Now to the Goths, as swift as swallow flies,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: There to dispose this treasure in mine arms,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And secretly to greet the empress’ friends.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Come on, you thick-lipped slave, I’ll bear you hence;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: For it is you that puts us to our shifts.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: I’ll make you feed on berries and on roots,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And feed on curds and whey, and suck the goat,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And cabin in a cave, and bring you up

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: To be a warrior and command a camp.
[_Exit._]
Enter Titus, old Marcus, his son Publius, Young Lucius, and other gentlemen with bows, and Titus bears the arrows with letters on the ends of them.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Come, Marcus, come. Kinsmen, this is the way.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Sir boy, let me see your archery.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Look ye draw home enough, and ’tis there straight.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: _Terras Astraea reliquit._

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Be you remembered, Marcus, she’s gone, she’s fled.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Sirs, take you to your tools. You, cousins, shall

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Go sound the ocean and cast your nets;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Happily you may catch her in the sea;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Yet there’s as little justice as at land.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: No; Publius and Sempronius, you must do it;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: ’Tis you must dig with mattock and with spade,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And pierce the inmost centre of the earth.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Then, when you come to Pluto’s region,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: I pray you, deliver him this petition;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Tell him it is for justice and for aid,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And that it comes from old Andronicus,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Shaken with sorrows in ungrateful Rome.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Ah, Rome! Well, well, I made thee miserable

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: What time I threw the people’s suffrages

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: On him that thus doth tyrannize o’er me.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Go, get you gone; and pray be careful all,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And leave you not a man-of-war unsearched.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: This wicked emperor may have shipped her hence;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And, kinsmen, then we may go pipe for justice.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: O Publius, is not this a heavy case,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: To see thy noble uncle thus distract?

lines.speaker: PUBLIUS
lines.text: Therefore, my lords, it highly us concerns

lines.speaker: PUBLIUS
lines.text: By day and night to attend him carefully,

lines.speaker: PUBLIUS
lines.text: And feed his humour kindly as we may,

lines.speaker: PUBLIUS
lines.text: Till time beget some careful remedy.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Kinsmen, his sorrows are past remedy,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: But . . . .

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Join with the Goths, and with revengeful war

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Take wreak on Rome for this ingratitude,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And vengeance on the traitor Saturnine.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Publius, how now? How now, my masters?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: What, have you met with her?

lines.speaker: PUBLIUS
lines.text: No, my good lord; but Pluto sends you word,

lines.speaker: PUBLIUS
lines.text: If you will have Revenge from hell, you shall.

lines.speaker: PUBLIUS
lines.text: Marry, for Justice, she is so employed,

lines.speaker: PUBLIUS
lines.text: He thinks, with Jove in heaven, or somewhere else,

lines.speaker: PUBLIUS
lines.text: So that perforce you must needs stay a time.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: He doth me wrong to feed me with delays.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: I’ll dive into the burning lake below,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And pull her out of Acheron by the heels.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Marcus, we are but shrubs, no cedars we,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: No big-boned men framed of the Cyclops’ size;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: But metal, Marcus, steel to the very back,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Yet wrung with wrongs more than our backs can bear;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And sith there’s no justice in earth nor hell,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: We will solicit heaven and move the gods

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: To send down Justice for to wreak our wrongs.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Come, to this gear. You are a good archer, Marcus.
[_He gives them the arrows._]

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: “_Ad Jovem,_” that’s for you; here, “_Ad Apollinem_”;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: “_Ad Martem,_” that’s for myself;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Here, boy, “to Pallas”; here, “to Mercury”;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: “To Saturn,” Caius, not to Saturnine;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: You were as good to shoot against the wind.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: To it, boy.—Marcus, loose when I bid.—

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Of my word, I have written to effect;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: There’s not a god left unsolicited.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Kinsmen, shoot all your shafts into the court.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: We will afflict the emperor in his pride.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Now, masters, draw. [_They shoot_.] O, well said, Lucius!

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Good boy, in Virgo’s lap! Give it Pallas.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: My lord, I aim a mile beyond the moon.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Your letter is with Jupiter by this.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Ha! ha! Publius, Publius, what hast thou done?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: See, see, thou hast shot off one of Taurus’ horns.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: This was the sport, my lord; when Publius shot,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: The Bull, being galled, gave Aries such a knock

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: That down fell both the Ram’s horns in the court;

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And who should find them but the empress’ villain?

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: She laughed, and told the Moor he should not choose

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: But give them to his master for a present.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Why, there it goes. God give his lordship joy!
Enter the Clown with a basket and two pigeons in it.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: News, news from heaven! Marcus, the post is come.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Sirrah, what tidings? Have you any letters?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Shall I have justice? What says Jupiter?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Ho, the gibbet-maker? He says that he hath taken them down again, for

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: the man must not be hanged till the next week.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: But what says Jupiter, I ask thee?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Alas, sir, I know not Jubiter; I never drank with him in all my life.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Why, villain, art not thou the carrier?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Ay, of my pigeons, sir; nothing else.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Why, didst thou not come from heaven?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: From heaven? Alas, sir, I never came there. God forbid I should be so

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: bold to press to heaven in my young days. Why, I am going with my

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: pigeons to the tribunal plebs, to take up a matter of brawl betwixt my

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: uncle and one of the emperal’s men.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Why, sir, that is as fit as can be to serve for your oration; and let

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: him deliver the pigeons to the emperor from you.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Tell me, can you deliver an oration to the emperor with a grace?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Nay, truly, sir, I could never say grace in all my life.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Sirrah, come hither. Make no more ado,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: But give your pigeons to the emperor.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: By me thou shalt have justice at his hands.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Hold, hold; meanwhile here’s money for thy charges.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Give me pen and ink.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Sirrah, can you with a grace deliver up a supplication?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Ay, sir.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Then here is a supplication for you. And when you come to him, at the

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: first approach you must kneel; then kiss his foot; then deliver up your

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: pigeons; and then look for your reward. I’ll be at hand, sir; see you

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: do it bravely.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: I warrant you, sir; let me alone.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Sirrah, hast thou a knife? Come let me see it.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Here, Marcus, fold it in the oration;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: For thou hast made it like a humble suppliant.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And when thou hast given it to the emperor,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Knock at my door, and tell me what he says.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: God be with you, sir; I will.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Come, Marcus, let us go. Publius, follow me.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Emperor Saturninus and Empress Tamora and her two sons Chiron and Demetrius, with Attendants. The Emperor brings the arrows in his hand that Titus shot at him.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Why, lords, what wrongs are these! Was ever seen

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: An emperor in Rome thus overborne,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Troubled, confronted thus; and, for the extent

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Of legal justice, used in such contempt?

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: My lords, you know, as know the mightful gods,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: However these disturbers of our peace

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Buzz in the people’s ears, there naught hath passed

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: But even with law against the wilful sons

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Of old Andronicus. And what an if

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: His sorrows have so overwhelmed his wits?

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Shall we be thus afflicted in his wreaks,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: His fits, his frenzy, and his bitterness?

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: And now he writes to heaven for his redress!

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: See, here’s “to Jove,” and this “to Mercury,”

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: This “to Apollo,” this to the god of war.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Sweet scrolls to fly about the streets of Rome!

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: What’s this but libelling against the senate,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: And blazoning our injustice everywhere?

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: A goodly humour, is it not, my lords?

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: As who would say, in Rome no justice were.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: But if I live, his feigned ecstasies

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Shall be no shelter to these outrages;

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: But he and his shall know that justice lives

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: In Saturninus’ health; whom, if she sleep,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: He’ll so awake as he in fury shall

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Cut off the proud’st conspirator that lives.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: My gracious lord, my lovely Saturnine,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Lord of my life, commander of my thoughts,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Calm thee, and bear the faults of Titus’ age,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Th’ effects of sorrow for his valiant sons,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Whose loss hath pierced him deep and scarred his heart;

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And rather comfort his distressed plight

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Than prosecute the meanest or the best

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: For these contempts. [_Aside_.] Why, thus it shall become

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: High-witted Tamora to gloze with all.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: But, Titus, I have touched thee to the quick;

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Thy life-blood out, if Aaron now be wise,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Then is all safe, the anchor in the port.
Enter Clown.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: How now, good fellow, wouldst thou speak with us?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Yes, forsooth, an your mistresship be emperial.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Empress I am, but yonder sits the emperor.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: ’Tis he. God and Saint Stephen give you good e’en. I have brought you a

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: letter and a couple of pigeons here.
[_Saturninus reads the letter._]

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Go take him away, and hang him presently.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: How much money must I have?

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Come, sirrah, you must be hanged.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Hanged! by’r Lady, then I have brought up a neck to a fair end.
[_Exit guarded._]

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Despiteful and intolerable wrongs!

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Shall I endure this monstrous villainy?

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: I know from whence this same device proceeds.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: May this be borne as if his traitorous sons,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: That died by law for murder of our brother,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Have by my means been butchered wrongfully?

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Go, drag the villain hither by the hair;

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Nor age nor honour shall shape privilege.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: For this proud mock I’ll be thy slaughterman,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Sly frantic wretch, that holp’st to make me great,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: In hope thyself should govern Rome and me.
Enter Aemilius.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: What news with thee, Aemilius?

lines.speaker: AEMILIUS
lines.text: Arm, my lord! Rome never had more cause.

lines.speaker: AEMILIUS
lines.text: The Goths have gathered head, and with a power

lines.speaker: AEMILIUS
lines.text: Of high-resolved men, bent to the spoil,

lines.speaker: AEMILIUS
lines.text: They hither march amain, under conduct

lines.speaker: AEMILIUS
lines.text: Of Lucius, son to old Andronicus;

lines.speaker: AEMILIUS
lines.text: Who threats, in course of this revenge, to do

lines.speaker: AEMILIUS
lines.text: As much as ever Coriolanus did.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Is warlike Lucius general of the Goths?

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: These tidings nip me, and I hang the head

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: As flowers with frost, or grass beat down with storms.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Ay, now begins our sorrows to approach.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: ’Tis he the common people love so much;

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Myself hath often overheard them say,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: When I have walked like a private man,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: That Lucius’ banishment was wrongfully,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: And they have wished that Lucius were their emperor.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Why should you fear? Is not your city strong?

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Ay, but the citizens favour Lucius,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: And will revolt from me to succour him.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: King, be thy thoughts imperious like thy name.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Is the sun dimmed, that gnats do fly in it?

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: The eagle suffers little birds to sing,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And is not careful what they mean thereby,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Knowing that with the shadow of his wings

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: He can at pleasure stint their melody;

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Even so mayest thou the giddy men of Rome.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Then cheer thy spirit; for know, thou emperor,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: I will enchant the old Andronicus

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: With words more sweet, and yet more dangerous,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Than baits to fish or honey-stalks to sheep,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Whenas the one is wounded with the bait,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: The other rotted with delicious feed.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: But he will not entreat his son for us.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: If Tamora entreat him, then he will,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: For I can smooth and fill his aged ears

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: With golden promises, that, were his heart

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Almost impregnable, his old ears deaf,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Yet should both ear and heart obey my tongue.
[_to Aemilius_]

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Go thou before, be our ambassador.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Say that the emperor requests a parley

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Of warlike Lucius, and appoint the meeting

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Even at his father’s house, the old Andronicus.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Aemilius, do this message honourably,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: And if he stand on hostage for his safety,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Bid him demand what pledge will please him best.

lines.speaker: AEMILIUS
lines.text: Your bidding shall I do effectually.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Now will I to that old Andronicus,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And temper him with all the art I have,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: To pluck proud Lucius from the warlike Goths.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And now, sweet emperor, be blithe again,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And bury all thy fear in my devices.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Then go successantly, and plead to him.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Lucius with an army of Goths, with drums and soldiers.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Approved warriors and my faithful friends,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: I have received letters from great Rome

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Which signifies what hate they bear their emperor

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And how desirous of our sight they are.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Therefore, great lords, be, as your titles witness,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Imperious, and impatient of your wrongs;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And wherein Rome hath done you any scath,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Let him make treble satisfaction.

lines.speaker: FIRST GOTH
lines.text: Brave slip, sprung from the great Andronicus,

lines.speaker: FIRST GOTH
lines.text: Whose name was once our terror, now our comfort,

lines.speaker: FIRST GOTH
lines.text: Whose high exploits and honourable deeds

lines.speaker: FIRST GOTH
lines.text: Ingrateful Rome requites with foul contempt,

lines.speaker: FIRST GOTH
lines.text: Be bold in us. We’ll follow where thou lead’st,

lines.speaker: FIRST GOTH
lines.text: Like stinging bees in hottest summer’s day

lines.speaker: FIRST GOTH
lines.text: Led by their master to the flowered fields,

lines.speaker: FIRST GOTH
lines.text: And be avenged on cursed Tamora.

lines.speaker: GOTHS
lines.text: And as he saith, so say we all with him.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: I humbly thank him, and I thank you all.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: But who comes here, led by a lusty Goth?
Enter a Goth, leading of Aaron with his Child in his arms.

lines.speaker: SECOND GOTH
lines.text: Renowned Lucius, from our troops I strayed

lines.speaker: SECOND GOTH
lines.text: To gaze upon a ruinous monastery;

lines.speaker: SECOND GOTH
lines.text: And as I earnestly did fix mine eye

lines.speaker: SECOND GOTH
lines.text: Upon the wasted building, suddenly

lines.speaker: SECOND GOTH
lines.text: I heard a child cry underneath a wall.

lines.speaker: SECOND GOTH
lines.text: I made unto the noise, when soon I heard

lines.speaker: SECOND GOTH
lines.text: The crying babe controlled with this discourse:

lines.speaker: SECOND GOTH
lines.text: “Peace, tawny slave, half me and half thy dame!

lines.speaker: SECOND GOTH
lines.text: Did not thy hue bewray whose brat thou art,

lines.speaker: SECOND GOTH
lines.text: Had nature lent thee but thy mother’s look,

lines.speaker: SECOND GOTH
