lines.text: Villain, thou mightst have been an emperor.

lines.speaker: SECOND GOTH
lines.text: But where the bull and cow are both milk-white,

lines.speaker: SECOND GOTH
lines.text: They never do beget a coal-black calf.

lines.speaker: SECOND GOTH
lines.text: Peace, villain, peace!” even thus he rates the babe,

lines.speaker: SECOND GOTH
lines.text: “For I must bear thee to a trusty Goth,

lines.speaker: SECOND GOTH
lines.text: Who, when he knows thou art the empress’ babe,

lines.speaker: SECOND GOTH
lines.text: Will hold thee dearly for thy mother’s sake.”

lines.speaker: SECOND GOTH
lines.text: With this, my weapon drawn, I rushed upon him,

lines.speaker: SECOND GOTH
lines.text: Surprised him suddenly, and brought him hither

lines.speaker: SECOND GOTH
lines.text: To use as you think needful of the man.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: O worthy Goth, this is the incarnate devil

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: That robbed Andronicus of his good hand;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: This is the pearl that pleased your empress’ eye;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And here’s the base fruit of her burning lust.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Say, wall-eyed slave, whither wouldst thou convey

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: This growing image of thy fiend-like face?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Why dost not speak? What, deaf? Not a word?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: A halter, soldiers, hang him on this tree,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And by his side his fruit of bastardy.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Touch not the boy, he is of royal blood.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Too like the sire for ever being good.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: First hang the child, that he may see it sprawl,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: A sight to vex the father’s soul withal.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Get me a ladder.
[_A ladder is brought, which Aaron is made to ascend._]

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Lucius, save the child;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And bear it from me to the empress.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: If thou do this, I’ll show thee wondrous things

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: That highly may advantage thee to hear.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: If thou wilt not, befall what may befall,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: I’ll speak no more but “Vengeance rot you all!”

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Say on, and if it please me which thou speak’st,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Thy child shall live, and I will see it nourished.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And if it please thee? Why, assure thee, Lucius,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: ’Twill vex thy soul to hear what I shall speak;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: For I must talk of murders, rapes, and massacres,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Acts of black night, abominable deeds,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Complots of mischief, treason, villainies,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Ruthful to hear, yet piteously performed.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And this shall all be buried in my death,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Unless thou swear to me my child shall live.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Tell on thy mind; I say thy child shall live.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Swear that he shall, and then I will begin.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Who should I swear by? Thou believ’st no god.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: That granted, how canst thou believe an oath?

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: What if I do not? As indeed I do not;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Yet, for I know thou art religious,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And hast a thing within thee called conscience,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: With twenty popish tricks and ceremonies

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Which I have seen thee careful to observe,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Therefore I urge thy oath; for that I know

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: An idiot holds his bauble for a god,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And keeps the oath which by that god he swears,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: To that I’ll urge him. Therefore thou shalt vow

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: By that same god, what god soe’er it be

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: That thou adorest and hast in reverence,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: To save my boy, to nourish and bring him up;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Or else I will discover naught to thee.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Even by my god I swear to thee I will.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: First know thou, I begot him on the empress.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: O most insatiate and luxurious woman!

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Tut, Lucius, this was but a deed of charity

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: To that which thou shalt hear of me anon.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: ’Twas her two sons that murdered Bassianus;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: They cut thy sister’s tongue, and ravished her,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And cut her hands, and trimmed her as thou sawest.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: O detestable villain, call’st thou that trimming?

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Why, she was washed, and cut, and trimmed; and ’twas

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Trim sport for them which had the doing of it.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: O barbarous beastly villains, like thyself!

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Indeed, I was their tutor to instruct them.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: That codding spirit had they from their mother,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: As sure a card as ever won the set;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: That bloody mind I think they learned of me,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: As true a dog as ever fought at head.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Well, let my deeds be witness of my worth.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: I trained thy brethren to that guileful hole

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Where the dead corpse of Bassianus lay.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: I wrote the letter that thy father found,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And hid the gold within that letter mentioned,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Confederate with the queen and her two sons.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And what not done, that thou hast cause to rue,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Wherein I had no stroke of mischief in’t?

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: I played the cheater for thy father’s hand,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And, when I had it, drew myself apart,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And almost broke my heart with extreme laughter.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: I pried me through the crevice of a wall

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: When, for his hand, he had his two sons’ heads;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Beheld his tears, and laughed so heartily

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: That both mine eyes were rainy like to his.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And when I told the empress of this sport,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: She sounded almost at my pleasing tale,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And for my tidings gave me twenty kisses.

lines.speaker: GOTH
lines.text: What, canst thou say all this and never blush?

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Ay, like a black dog, as the saying is.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Art thou not sorry for these heinous deeds?

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Ay, that I had not done a thousand more.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Even now I curse the day, and yet, I think,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Few come within the compass of my curse,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Wherein I did not some notorious ill,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: As kill a man, or else devise his death;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Ravish a maid, or plot the way to do it;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Accuse some innocent, and forswear myself;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Set deadly enmity between two friends;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Make poor men’s cattle break their necks;

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Set fire on barns and haystalks in the night,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And bid the owners quench them with their tears.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Oft have I digged up dead men from their graves,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And set them upright at their dear friends’ door,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Even when their sorrows almost was forgot,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And on their skins, as on the bark of trees,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Have with my knife carved in Roman letters,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: “Let not your sorrow die, though I am dead.”

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: But I have done a thousand dreadful things

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: As willingly as one would kill a fly,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And nothing grieves me heartily indeed

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: But that I cannot do ten thousand more.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Bring down the devil, for he must not die

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: So sweet a death as hanging presently.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: If there be devils, would I were a devil,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: To live and burn in everlasting fire,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: So I might have your company in hell

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: But to torment you with my bitter tongue!

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Sirs, stop his mouth, and let him speak no more.
Enter Aemilius.

lines.speaker: GOTH
lines.text: My lord, there is a messenger from Rome

lines.speaker: GOTH
lines.text: Desires to be admitted to your presence.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Let him come near.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Welcome, Aemilius. What’s the news from Rome?

lines.speaker: AEMILIUS
lines.text: Lord Lucius, and you princes of the Goths,

lines.speaker: AEMILIUS
lines.text: The Roman emperor greets you all by me;

lines.speaker: AEMILIUS
lines.text: And, for he understands you are in arms,

lines.speaker: AEMILIUS
lines.text: He craves a parley at your father’s house,

lines.speaker: AEMILIUS
lines.text: Willing you to demand your hostages,

lines.speaker: AEMILIUS
lines.text: And they shall be immediately delivered.

lines.speaker: FIRST GOTH
lines.text: What says our general?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Aemilius, let the emperor give his pledges

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Unto my father and my uncle Marcus,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And we will come. March away.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Tamora and her two sons, disguised.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Thus, in this strange and sad habiliment,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: I will encounter with Andronicus,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And say I am Revenge, sent from below

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: To join with him and right his heinous wrongs.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Knock at his study, where they say he keeps

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: To ruminate strange plots of dire revenge;

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Tell him Revenge is come to join with him

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And work confusion on his enemies.
[_They knock._]

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Titus above opens his study door.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Who doth molest my contemplation?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Is it your trick to make me ope the door,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: That so my sad decrees may fly away

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And all my study be to no effect?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: You are deceived; for what I mean to do

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: See here in bloody lines I have set down;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And what is written shall be executed.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Titus, I am come to talk with thee.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: No, not a word; how can I grace my talk,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Wanting a hand to give it action?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Thou hast the odds of me; therefore no more.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: If thou didst know me, thou wouldst talk with me.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: I am not mad; I know thee well enough.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Witness this wretched stump, witness these crimson lines;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Witness these trenches made by grief and care;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Witness the tiring day and heavy night;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Witness all sorrow that I know thee well

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: For our proud empress, mighty Tamora.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Is not thy coming for my other hand?

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Know thou, sad man, I am not Tamora;

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: She is thy enemy, and I thy friend.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: I am Revenge, sent from th’ infernal kingdom

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: To ease the gnawing vulture of thy mind

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: By working wreakful vengeance on thy foes.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Come down and welcome me to this world’s light;

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Confer with me of murder and of death.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: There’s not a hollow cave or lurking-place,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: No vast obscurity or misty vale,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Where bloody murder or detested rape

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Can couch for fear but I will find them out,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And in their ears tell them my dreadful name,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Revenge, which makes the foul offender quake.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Art thou Revenge? And art thou sent to me

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: To be a torment to mine enemies?

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: I am; therefore come down and welcome me.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Do me some service ere I come to thee.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Lo, by thy side where Rape and Murder stands;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Now give some surance that thou art Revenge:

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Stab them, or tear them on thy chariot wheels,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And then I’ll come and be thy waggoner,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And whirl along with thee about the globe.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Provide thee two proper palfreys, black as jet,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: To hale thy vengeful waggon swift away,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And find out murderers in their guilty caves.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And when thy car is loaden with their heads,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: I will dismount, and by the waggon-wheel

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Trot like a servile footman all day long,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Even from Hyperion’s rising in the east

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Until his very downfall in the sea.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And day by day I’ll do this heavy task,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: So thou destroy Rapine and Murder there.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: These are my ministers, and come with me.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Are they thy ministers? What are they called?

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Rapine and Murder; therefore called so

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: ’Cause they take vengeance of such kind of men.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Good Lord, how like the empress’ sons they are,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And you the empress! But we worldly men

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Have miserable, mad, mistaking eyes.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: O sweet Revenge, now do I come to thee;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And, if one arm’s embracement will content thee,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: I will embrace thee in it by and by.
[_He exits above._]

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: This closing with him fits his lunacy.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Whate’er I forge to feed his brain-sick humours,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Do you uphold and maintain in your speeches,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: For now he firmly takes me for Revenge;

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And, being credulous in this mad thought,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: I’ll make him send for Lucius his son;

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And whilst I at a banquet hold him sure,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: I’ll find some cunning practice out of hand

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: To scatter and disperse the giddy Goths,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Or, at the least, make them his enemies.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: See, here he comes, and I must ply my theme.
Enter Titus.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Long have I been forlorn, and all for thee.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Welcome, dread Fury, to my woeful house.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Rapine and Murder, you are welcome too.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: How like the empress and her sons you are!

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Well are you fitted, had you but a Moor.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Could not all hell afford you such a devil?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: For well I wot the empress never wags

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: But in her company there is a Moor;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And, would you represent our queen aright,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: It were convenient you had such a devil.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: But welcome as you are. What shall we do?

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: What wouldst thou have us do, Andronicus?

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Show me a murderer, I’ll deal with him.

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: Show me a villain that hath done a rape,

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: And I am sent to be revenged on him.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Show me a thousand that hath done thee wrong,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And I will be revenged on them all.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Look round about the wicked streets of Rome,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And when thou find’st a man that’s like thyself,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Good Murder, stab him; he’s a murderer.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Go thou with him; and when it is thy hap

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: To find another that is like to thee,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Good Rapine, stab him; he is a ravisher.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Go thou with them; and in the emperor’s court

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: There is a queen, attended by a Moor;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Well shalt thou know her by thine own proportion,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: For up and down she doth resemble thee.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: I pray thee, do on them some violent death;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: They have been violent to me and mine.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Well hast thou lessoned us; this shall we do.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: But would it please thee, good Andronicus,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: To send for Lucius, thy thrice-valiant son,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Who leads towards Rome a band of warlike Goths,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And bid him come and banquet at thy house?

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: When he is here, even at thy solemn feast,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: I will bring in the empress and her sons,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: The emperor himself, and all thy foes,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And at thy mercy shall they stoop and kneel,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And on them shalt thou ease thy angry heart.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: What says Andronicus to this device?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Marcus, my brother, ’tis sad Titus calls.
Enter Marcus.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Go, gentle Marcus, to thy nephew Lucius;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Thou shalt inquire him out among the Goths.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Bid him repair to me and bring with him

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Some of the chiefest princes of the Goths;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Bid him encamp his soldiers where they are.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Tell him the emperor and the empress too

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Feast at my house, and he shall feast with them.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: This do thou for my love; and so let him,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: As he regards his aged father’s life.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: This will I do, and soon return again.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Now will I hence about thy business,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And take my ministers along with me.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Nay, nay, let Rape and Murder stay with me,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Or else I’ll call my brother back again

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And cleave to no revenge but Lucius.
[_Aside to them_.]

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: What say you, boys? Will you abide with him,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Whiles I go tell my lord the emperor

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: How I have governed our determined jest?

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Yield to his humour, smooth and speak him fair,

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: And tarry with him till I come again.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: I knew them all, though they suppose me mad,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And will o’erreach them in their own devices,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: A pair of cursed hell-hounds and their dam.

lines.speaker: DEMETRIUS
lines.text: Madam, depart at pleasure; leave us here.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Farewell, Andronicus. Revenge now goes

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: To lay a complot to betray thy foes.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: I know thou dost; and, sweet Revenge, farewell.
[_Exit Tamora._]

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: Tell us, old man, how shall we be employed?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Tut, I have work enough for you to do.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Publius, come hither, Caius, and Valentine.
Enter Publius and others.

lines.speaker: PUBLIUS
lines.text: What is your will?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Know you these two?

lines.speaker: PUBLIUS
lines.text: The empress’ sons, I take them, Chiron, Demetrius.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Fie, Publius, fie, thou art too much deceived.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: The one is Murder, and Rape is the other’s name;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And therefore bind them, gentle Publius.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Caius and Valentine, lay hands on them.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Oft have you heard me wish for such an hour,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And now I find it. Therefore bind them sure,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And stop their mouths if they begin to cry.
[_Exit Titus._]

lines.speaker: CHIRON
lines.text: Villains, forbear! We are the empress’ sons.

lines.speaker: PUBLIUS
lines.text: And therefore do we what we are commanded.

lines.speaker: PUBLIUS
lines.text: Stop close their mouths, let them not speak a word.

lines.speaker: PUBLIUS
lines.text: Is he sure bound? Look that you bind them fast.
Enter Titus Andronicus with a knife, and Lavinia with a basin.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Come, come, Lavinia; look, thy foes are bound.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Sirs, stop their mouths, let them not speak to me,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: But let them hear what fearful words I utter.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: O villains, Chiron and Demetrius!

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Here stands the spring whom you have stained with mud,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: This goodly summer with your winter mixed.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: You killed her husband, and for that vile fault

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Two of her brothers were condemned to death,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: My hand cut off and made a merry jest,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Both her sweet hands, her tongue, and that more dear

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Than hands or tongue, her spotless chastity,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Inhuman traitors, you constrained and forced.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: What would you say if I should let you speak?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Villains, for shame you could not beg for grace.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Hark, wretches, how I mean to martyr you.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: This one hand yet is left to cut your throats,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Whiles that Lavinia ’tween her stumps doth hold

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: The basin that receives your guilty blood.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: You know your mother means to feast with me,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And calls herself Revenge, and thinks me mad.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Hark, villains! I will grind your bones to dust,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And with your blood and it I’ll make a paste,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And of the paste a coffin I will rear,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And make two pasties of your shameful heads,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And bid that strumpet, your unhallowed dam,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Like to the earth swallow her own increase.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: This is the feast that I have bid her to,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And this the banquet she shall surfeit on;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: For worse than Philomel you used my daughter,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And worse than Procne I will be revenged.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And now prepare your throats.—Lavinia, come

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Receive the blood.
[_He cuts their throats._]

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And when that they are dead,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Let me go grind their bones to powder small,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And with this hateful liquor temper it,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And in that paste let their vile heads be baked.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Come, come, be everyone officious

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: To make this banquet, which I wish may prove

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: More stern and bloody than the Centaurs’ feast.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: So, now bring them in, for I’ll play the cook,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And see them ready against their mother comes.
[_Exeunt, carrying the dead bodies._]

scenes.setting: Rome. A Pavilion in Titus’s Gardens, with tables, &c.

lines.text: Enter Lucius, Marcus and the Goths, with Aaron, prisoner.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Uncle Marcus, since ’tis my father’s mind

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: That I repair to Rome, I am content.

lines.speaker: FIRST GOTH
lines.text: And ours with thine, befall what fortune will.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Good uncle, take you in this barbarous Moor,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: This ravenous tiger, this accursed devil;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Let him receive no sust’nance, fetter him,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Till he be brought unto the empress’ face

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: For testimony of her foul proceedings.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And see the ambush of our friends be strong;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: I fear the emperor means no good to us.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Some devil whisper curses in my ear,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: And prompt me that my tongue may utter forth

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: The venomous malice of my swelling heart!

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Away, inhuman dog, unhallowed slave!

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Sirs, help our uncle to convey him in.
[_Sound trumpets._]

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: The trumpets show the emperor is at hand.
[_Exeunt Goths with Aaron._]
Enter Emperor Saturninus and Empress Tamora with Aemilius, Tribunes and others.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: What, hath the firmament more suns than one?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: What boots it thee to call thyself a sun?

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Rome’s emperor, and nephew, break the parle;

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: These quarrels must be quietly debated.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: The feast is ready which the careful Titus

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Hath ordained to an honourable end,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: For peace, for love, for league, and good to Rome.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Please you, therefore, draw nigh and take your places.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Marcus, we will.
Trumpets sounding, enter Titus like a cook, placing the dishes, with Young Lucius and others, and Lavinia with a veil over her face.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Welcome, my lord; welcome, dread queen;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Welcome, ye warlike Goths; welcome, Lucius;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And welcome all. Although the cheer be poor,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: ’Twill fill your stomachs; please you eat of it.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Why art thou thus attired, Andronicus?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Because I would be sure to have all well

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: To entertain your highness and your empress.

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: We are beholden to you, good Andronicus.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: An if your highness knew my heart, you were.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: My lord the emperor, resolve me this:

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Was it well done of rash Virginius

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: To slay his daughter with his own right hand,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Because she was enforced, stained, and deflowered?

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: It was, Andronicus.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Your reason, mighty lord?

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Because the girl should not survive her shame,

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: And by her presence still renew his sorrows.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: A reason mighty, strong, and effectual;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: A pattern, precedent, and lively warrant

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: For me, most wretched, to perform the like.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Die, die, Lavinia, and thy shame with thee;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And with thy shame thy father’s sorrow die!
[_He kills Lavinia._]

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: What hast thou done, unnatural and unkind?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Killed her for whom my tears have made me blind.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: I am as woeful as Virginius was,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And have a thousand times more cause than he

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: To do this outrage, and it now is done.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: What, was she ravished? Tell who did the deed.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Will’t please you eat? Will’t please your highness feed?

lines.speaker: TAMORA
lines.text: Why hast thou slain thine only daughter thus?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Not I; ’twas Chiron and Demetrius.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: They ravished her, and cut away her tongue;

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And they, ’twas they, that did her all this wrong.

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Go fetch them hither to us presently.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Why, there they are, both baked in that pie,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Whereof their mother daintily hath fed,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Eating the flesh that she herself hath bred.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: ’Tis true, ’tis true; witness my knife’s sharp point.
[_He stabs the Empress._]

lines.speaker: SATURNINUS
lines.text: Die, frantic wretch, for this accursed deed.
[_He kills Titus._]

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Can the son’s eye behold his father bleed?
[_He kills Saturninus._]

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: There’s meed for meed, death for a deadly deed.
[_A great tumult. Lucius, Marcus, and others go aloft to the upper stage._]

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: You sad-faced men, people and sons of Rome,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: By uproar severed, as a flight of fowl

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Scattered by winds and high tempestuous gusts,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: O, let me teach you how to knit again

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: This scattered corn into one mutual sheaf,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: These broken limbs again into one body;

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Lest Rome herself be bane unto herself,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And she whom mighty kingdoms curtsy to,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Like a forlorn and desperate castaway,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Do shameful execution on herself.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: But if my frosty signs and chaps of age,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Grave witnesses of true experience,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Cannot induce you to attend my words,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Speak, Rome’s dear friend, [_to Lucius_] as erst our ancestor,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: When with his solemn tongue he did discourse

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: To love-sick Dido’s sad attending ear

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: The story of that baleful burning night

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: When subtle Greeks surprised King Priam’s Troy.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Tell us what Sinon hath bewitched our ears,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Or who hath brought the fatal engine in

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: That gives our Troy, our Rome, the civil wound.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: My heart is not compact of flint nor steel,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Nor can I utter all our bitter grief,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: But floods of tears will drown my oratory

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And break my utterance, even in the time

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: When it should move you to attend me most,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And force you to commiseration.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Here’s Rome’s young captain, let him tell the tale,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: While I stand by and weep to hear him speak.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Then, noble auditory, be it known to you

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: That Chiron and the damned Demetrius

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Were they that murdered our emperor’s brother;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And they it were that ravished our sister.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: For their fell faults our brothers were beheaded,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Our father’s tears despised, and basely cozened

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Of that true hand that fought Rome’s quarrel out

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And sent her enemies unto the grave.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Lastly, myself unkindly banished,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: The gates shut on me, and turned weeping out,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: To beg relief among Rome’s enemies;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Who drowned their enmity in my true tears,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And oped their arms to embrace me as a friend.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: I am the turned-forth, be it known to you,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: That have preserved her welfare in my blood

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And from her bosom took the enemy’s point,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Sheathing the steel in my advent’rous body.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Alas, you know I am no vaunter, I;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: My scars can witness, dumb although they are,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: That my report is just and full of truth.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: But soft, methinks I do digress too much,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Citing my worthless praise. O, pardon me;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: For when no friends are by, men praise themselves.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Now is my turn to speak. Behold the child.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Of this was Tamora delivered,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: The issue of an irreligious Moor,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Chief architect and plotter of these woes.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: The villain is alive in Titus’ house,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And as he is to witness, this is true.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Now judge what cause had Titus to revenge

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: These wrongs unspeakable, past patience,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Or more than any living man could bear.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Now have you heard the truth. What say you, Romans?

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Have we done aught amiss? Show us wherein,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And, from the place where you behold us pleading,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: The poor remainder of Andronici

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Will, hand in hand, all headlong hurl ourselves,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And on the ragged stones beat forth our souls,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And make a mutual closure of our house.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Speak, Romans, speak, and if you say we shall,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Lo, hand in hand, Lucius and I will fall.

lines.speaker: AEMILIUS
lines.text: Come, come, thou reverend man of Rome,

lines.speaker: AEMILIUS
lines.text: And bring our emperor gently in thy hand,

lines.speaker: AEMILIUS
lines.text: Lucius our emperor; for well I know

lines.speaker: AEMILIUS
lines.text: The common voice do cry it shall be so.

lines.speaker: ROMANS
lines.text: Lucius, all hail, Rome’s royal emperor!

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Go, go into old Titus’ sorrowful house,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: And hither hale that misbelieving Moor

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: To be adjudged some direful slaught’ring death,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: As punishment for his most wicked life.
[_Exeunt Attendants. Lucius and Marcus come down from the upper stage._]

lines.speaker: ROMANS
lines.text: Lucius, all hail, Rome’s gracious governor!

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Thanks, gentle Romans. May I govern so

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: To heal Rome’s harms and wipe away her woe!

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: But, gentle people, give me aim awhile,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: For nature puts me to a heavy task.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Stand all aloof; but, uncle, draw you near

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: To shed obsequious tears upon this trunk.
[_He kisses Titus._]

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: O, take this warm kiss on thy pale cold lips.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: These sorrowful drops upon thy blood-stained face,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: The last true duties of thy noble son.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Tear for tear and loving kiss for kiss

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Thy brother Marcus tenders on thy lips.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: O, were the sum of these that I should pay

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Countless and infinite, yet would I pay them.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Come hither, boy; come, come, and learn of us

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: To melt in showers. Thy grandsire loved thee well.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Many a time he danced thee on his knee,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Sung thee asleep, his loving breast thy pillow;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Many a story hath he told to thee,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And bid thee bear his pretty tales in mind

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And talk of them when he was dead and gone.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: How many thousand times hath these poor lips,

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: When they were living, warmed themselves on thine!

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: O, now, sweet boy, give them their latest kiss.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Bid him farewell; commit him to the grave.

lines.speaker: MARCUS
lines.text: Do them that kindness, and take leave of them.

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: O grandsire, grandsire, e’en with all my heart

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: Would I were dead, so you did live again!

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: O Lord, I cannot speak to him for weeping;

lines.speaker: YOUNG LUCIUS
lines.text: My tears will choke me if I ope my mouth.
Re-enter Attendants with Aaron.

lines.speaker: AEMILIUS
lines.text: You sad Andronici, have done with woes.

lines.speaker: AEMILIUS
lines.text: Give sentence on the execrable wretch

lines.speaker: AEMILIUS
lines.text: That hath been breeder of these dire events.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Set him breast-deep in earth and famish him;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: There let him stand and rave and cry for food.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: If anyone relieves or pities him,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: For the offence he dies. This is our doom.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Some stay to see him fastened in the earth.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Ah, why should wrath be mute and fury dumb?

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: I am no baby, I, that with base prayers

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: I should repent the evils I have done.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Ten thousand worse than ever yet I did

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: Would I perform, if I might have my will.

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: If one good deed in all my life I did,

lines.speaker: AARON
lines.text: I do repent it from my very soul.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Some loving friends convey the emperor hence,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And give him burial in his father’s grave.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: My father and Lavinia shall forthwith

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Be closed in our household’s monument.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: As for that ravenous tiger, Tamora,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: No funeral rite, nor man in mournful weed,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: No mournful bell shall ring her burial;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: But throw her forth to beasts and birds of prey.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Her life was beastly and devoid of pity;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And being dead, let birds on her take pity.
[_Exeunt._]
